ideal_interaction: Tap each manifest line against its crate tag on the bay list, flagging any line that does not match, and run the purge only after every line is checked.

label: Stand by for emergency beam-out
human_steps: Sit at the transporter console and confirm the emergency pattern is loaded.
Read the emergency beam-out checklist and confirm the emergency channel is open.
Keep the cover over the emergency lock button closed while standing by.
Watch the standby light and the comm for the bridge's emergency call.
On the call, flip the cover up, confirm the target, and press energize.
Log the time the call arrived and the time the beam-out ran.
what_makes_it_hard: Staying alert through long idle stretches and reacting in seconds when the call comes, since a late beam-out leaves patients stuck in a hazard.
ideal_interaction: Keep the emergency lock cover closed while waiting, and when the bridge call sounds, flip the cover up and press energize before the standby timer runs out.
fit_note: Calibrate is a tuning game; standby is vigilance and a fast physical response to a call.

label: Beam patients direct to sickbay
human_steps: Read the sickbay bed grid coordinates and the patient count from medical.
Walk to the pad and place each stretcher on its marked spot.
Confirm each patient's beacon ID matches the triage tag clipped to the stretcher.
Enter the sickbay coordinates and read them against the medical sheet.
Start the beam and watch the bed sensor tally for arrivals.
Call sickbay to confirm each patient has arrived.
what_makes_it_hard: Matching each stretcher to its triage tag, since a swapped patient arriving at the wrong bed is a clinical error.
ideal_interaction: Set each stretcher on its numbered pad spot, then enter the sickbay coordinates and press energize only after the beacon on each tag matches its bed number.

label: Decontaminate buffer
human_steps: Put on gloves and walk to the buffer console with the decon kit.
Lock the buffer and open its decon port.
Pour decon solution into the port until it reaches the full line on the tank.
Run the flush cycle and watch the effluent light change from amber to clear.
Wipe the port rim with a disinfectant cloth and bag the cloth.
Log the decon cycle and close the port with its seal.
what_makes_it_hard: Knowing the effluent is truly clear and not just diluted, since leftover contamination spreads to the next patients.
ideal_interaction: Pour decon into the port until it reaches the marked line, then keep the flush lever pressed while the effluent light runs from amber toward clear.
fit_note: Calibrate is a tuning game; decontamination is a physical flush and wipe at the port.

label: Full transporter system test
human_steps: Read the test script on the console and confirm the transporter is in test mode.
Run the buffer self-test and note its pass result.
Run the emitter self-test and watch each coil's test pulse.
Run the lock self-test with the beacon and check the lock light.
Listen to the cooling fan and check coil temperatures through the cycle.
Log each subsystem result and the overall test status.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a passing self-test from a subsystem that passes when cold but drifts once warm.
ideal_interaction: Walk the test sequence on the console, pressing each self-test button in order and watching the lock light and the coil temperature bar rise and settle.

label: Test pad-to-pad transfer with inert mass
human_steps: Place the inert mass block on the source pad and check its marking.
Walk to the destination pad and clear it of loose items.
Enter the pad-to-pad transfer coordinates on the console.
Start the transfer and watch the source pad mass count go to zero.
Walk to the destination pad and read the block's weight on its load plate.
Compare the destination weight to the source reading and log any loss.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging whether the mass arrives intact, since a small loss or shift in the block signals a pattern fault the console may not report.
ideal_interaction: Start the transfer on the console, then carry the inert block from the source pad to the destination load plate and check its mass reading matches the source.

label: Report results to ops
human_steps: Gather the test logs from the console and the lock log from the lab tray.
Read each subsystem result and mark it pass, fail, or conditional.
Write each failure with its subsystem name, reading, and test step number.
Attach the lock log and the pad transfer weights to the report.
Check the total test count against the number of steps in the script.
Send the report to ops and log the submission time.
what_makes_it_hard: Recording the real reading and step number for each failure instead of a vague summary, since ops cannot act on 'some issues'.
ideal_interaction: Fill the report form field by field, typing each subsystem reading next to its test step number, and press submit only when the tally at the bottom matches the script count.

label: Pad and emitter diagnostic
human_steps: Walk to pad two with the tech kit and check the floor for loose debris.
Fit the emitter probe into its test port and set the sweep to fast mode.
Watch the emitter waveform and count the peaks in each band.
Check the buffer integrity light on the pad's side panel.
Note on the sheet any peak that runs wide or late.
Log the pad state and tell the chief the pad is green.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a late or wide peak from a normal one, since a wide or late peak means an emitter is starting to fail.
ideal_interaction: Seat the emitter probe in its port, then tap each peak on the waveform in turn and tag any peak that lands outside its band.

label: Flush pattern buffer
human_steps: Check the console lock indicator is dark, meaning no beam is in progress.
Open the buffer flush cover and press the flush key.
Watch the buffer fill gauge fall to the empty mark.
Send a blank pattern and read the echo on the display.
Confirm the echo is empty and no residue lights appear.
Close the flush cover and log the flush time.
what_makes_it_hard: Confirming the buffer is truly clear from the echo, since a faint leftover pattern passes the gauge but shows up in the next beam.
ideal_interaction: Press the flush key and keep it down until the fill gauge drops to empty, then send the blank pattern and read the echo for residue lights.

label: Coil wear check and swap
human_steps: Carry the coil spares tray to the workbench and set the coil fixture in its clamp.
Unlatch the pad two coil access panel and lift out the old coil with the coil puller.
Measure the coil wire diameter with the micrometer and check resistance with the meter.
Compare the readings to the wear limit stamped on the coil ring.
If over limit, seat the spare coil and torque the retaining nut to spec.
Run the coil test and log the swap.
what_makes_it_hard: Deciding whether a coil reading just inside the limit is safe, since a coil at the edge of its limit fails mid-beam.
ideal_interaction: Clamp the coil in the fixture, set the micrometer on the wire and read it, and swap the coil only when the reading crosses the stamped limit.

label: Check power feed from junction
human_steps: Walk to the transporter junction box and open the feed inspection hatch.
Clip the voltmeter leads onto the feed test points.
Read the feed voltage and compare it to the baseline sticker on the box.
Switch the coil load on and watch the voltage for one full cycle.
If the voltage sags below the band, radio EPS with the reading.
Log the feed reading and close the hatch.
what_makes_it_hard: Catching a voltage sag that appears only under load, since a static reading looks fine while the coils are cold.
ideal_interaction: Clip the voltmeter leads to the test points, then hold the coil load switch on and watch the voltage needle for any dip.

label: Full pad diagnostic
human_steps: Walk to pad one and plug the pad test rig into the wall outlet.
Set the rig to full diagnostic mode and clamp the probe to the pad edge.
Run each of the four pad test patterns in turn and note the pass light.
Inspect the surface plates for hairline cracks with a magnifier.
Check the rig log for any pattern that passed only on a retry.
Save the diagnostic report to the pad file.
what_makes_it_hard: Catching a pattern that passes only on the second try, since a retry-pass means the pad fails intermittently and will fail on a real beam.
ideal_interaction: Clamp the probe to the pad edge and cycle the four patterns with the selector, pressing test for each and checking whether the pass light holds on the first press.

label: Coil and buffer maintenance
human_steps: Lay the coil cleaning kit out on the workbench and unplug the buffer unit.
Remove the coil cover and brush the windings with a dry brush.
Inspect the buffer cable connectors for corrosion or bent pins.
Reseat each connector and turn its thumb screw until firm.
Power the buffer up and listen for a steady fan hum.
Write the maintenance date on the coil tag.
what_makes_it_hard: Seating each connector fully without cross-threading, since a connector left half a turn loose works until the next high load.
ideal_interaction: Turn each thumb screw down with the driver and stop at the first firm resistance, then watch the fan hum hold steady after power-up.

label: Pre-load surveyor pads and lock beacon
human_steps: Pick the survey pads from the rack and check each beacon's battery indicator.
Walk to the transporter pad and set each survey pad on its marker.
Enter the survey coordinates into the pad console grid.
Clip the lock beacon onto the team leader's tricorder strap.
Check the console's lock preview shows the correct beacon ID on each pad.
Report the pads loaded and their beacon IDs to the chief.
what_makes_it_hard: Getting each beacon ID onto the right pad, since two beacons on one channel make the lock resolve to the wrong person.
ideal_interaction: Set each survey pad on its marker, then type its coordinates into the grid and wait for the lock preview to show the correct beacon ID before moving on.

label: Hold standby lock on away team
human_steps: Put the standby lock on the away team's beacon and read the lock status on the console.
Watch the range bar against the team's movement reports.
Check the team's last position on the map matches the beacon's position.
Listen on the comm link for drop-out tones.
If a beacon fades, switch to the backup beacon.
Record the lock times and any switch on the standby log.
what_makes_it_hard: Recognizing a beacon drifting before it drops, since a lost beacon means the team cannot be pulled out.
ideal_interaction: Watch the range bar and the team's map dot together, and press the backup beacon button the instant the bar dips below its marked level, then wait for the lock to read steady.
fit_note: Calibrate tunes a lock; the real job is steady monitoring of beacons and switching to backup when one fades.

label: Beam samples to lab
human_steps: Collect the labeled sample containers from the surveyor's rack and read each label.
Set the containers on the outgoing pad's marker in order of their label numbers.
Enter the lab coordinates on the console and read each digit before entering it.
Check each container is sealed and no lid is cracked.
Press energize for the sample beam and watch the pad counter tick once per container.
Confirm arrival with the lab and log the sample IDs.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping each sample's label matched to its container, since a swapped sample corrupts the whole study.
ideal_interaction: Set each labeled container on the pad marker in number order, then enter the lab coordinates and press energize while the counter ticks once per container.

label: Verify pad weight limits and cargo manifest
human_steps: Read the manifest's total weight and the pad's rated limit on the placard.
Walk to the pad and place a weight tester on each pad corner.
Read each corner weight and add them up on the console.
Compare the total and the heaviest single crate against the limit.
Flag any batch over limit and split it on the manifest.
Sign the weight check and send the batch to the cargo bay.
what_makes_it_hard: Splitting batches so no single corner is overloaded, since an unbalanced pad drops a crate mid-beam.
ideal_interaction: Set the weight testers on each pad corner in turn, then drag the crate blocks on the console's pad diagram until all four corners read within the limit band.

label: Beam cargo crates in batches
human_steps: Walk the first batch of crates to the pad on a hand truck.
Tilt each crate down onto its numbered pad spot and check it sits flat.
Stand clear of the pad edge and confirm the pad shows the batch is ready.
Start the batch beam from the console and wait for the transfer tone.
Walk to the cargo bay and count the crates that landed from the batch.
Repeat for each batch and log the crate count per batch.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping crates from sliding on the pad during batch loading, since one sliding crate misaligns the whole beam.
ideal_interaction: Walk each crate on the hand truck to its numbered spot and tilt it down flat, then trigger batch start only when every spot shows a flat crate.
fit_note: Load balancing is what the game models; the real work is physically loading crates batch by batch with a hand truck.

label: Reconcile arrivals with cargo bay
human_steps: Walk to the cargo bay door and check the arrivals light shows the batch arrived.
Walk along the bay row and touch each crate lid in turn to confirm it has landed.
Read the crate ID stencil on each lid and tick it off the arrivals list.
Check the arrivals list against the manifest for any unticked line.
Mark any missing crate with a red tag on the bay door.
Send the reconciled count to the chief.
what_makes_it_hard: Finding a missing crate before the beam window closes, since an unaccounted crate usually surfaces only after the bay has been cleared.
ideal_interaction: Walk the bay row touching each crate lid and tick its stencil line on the arrivals list, stopping whenever a stencil is missing from the manifest.

label: Clear pads and hold lock on casualty group
human_steps: Walk to each pad and clear loose debris or dropped tools from its platform.
Run a flat hand along each pad edge to check for damage or rubble.
Walk back to the console and read the casualty beacon roster.
Lock the group's beacons in order of triage color.
Watch each lock light and call out any that flicker.
Confirm the group is clear and holding lock to the bridge over comm.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding a lock on casualties whose beacons weaken at different rates, since losing one beacon strands a patient on the pad.
ideal_interaction: Walk each pad and sweep debris off with the brush, then lock the beacons by triage color and keep each lock light steady until the bridge confirms.
fit_note: Calibrate tunes a lock; clearing pads and calling out flickering beacons are separate physical and monitoring tasks.

label: Beam patients direct to sickbay
human_steps: Hear the sickbay bed call and read the patient list with bed numbers.
Walk to the pad and check each patient is on a stretcher with a visible tag.
Seat the stretcher transport strap into the pad clamp.
Enter the bed coordinate for the first patient.
Energize and watch the patient counter on the bed panel.
Confirm each patient's arrival on sickbay comm and log their bed.
what_makes_it_hard: Getting each patient to their assigned bed, since a patient sent to the wrong bed in triage means delayed treatment.
ideal_interaction: Clip the transport strap into the pad clamp, then enter the bed coordinate and hold energize until the bed panel shows the patient in the correct bed.

label: Beam medical supplies out
human_steps: Pull the supply order from the medical requisition clipboard.
Walk to the supply cabinet and gather each item named on the order.
Pack the items into the relief kit and check the seal tape.
Place the kit on the pad's marked center spot.
Enter the relief team coordinates and read them back.
Energize and confirm the kit arrival tone on the relief team comm.
what_makes_it_hard: Packing every item on the order, since the relief team cannot improvise a missing dose.
ideal_interaction: Pick each requisition item from the cabinet and tap it into the kit in order, then seal the kit before energizing the beam.

label: Run full transporter test cycle
human_steps: Walk onto the test pad and clear the marker spot of tools.
Run the pad built-in self-test and read the lamp status.
Step to the inner ring and check each emitter seal.
Start the test cycle from the console and return to the pad.
Watch the cycle pattern readout for any error code.
Note any error code on the test sheet and reset the pad.
what_makes_it_hard: Recognizing a cycle error code that looks harmless, since one code can mean the pattern lock is intermittent.
ideal_interaction: Stand on the inner ring and press each emitter seal in turn, then start the cycle and read the pattern readout line by line for error codes.

label: Test emergency lock with a weighted dummy load
human_steps: Heave the weighted dummy from the rack onto the hand dolly.
Wheel the dummy to the test pad and lift it onto the marked center.
Engage the emergency lock with the manual key switch on the pad rail.
Watch the lock gauge and the dummy for any tilt.
Hold the lock for the full timed period and check the dummy has not shifted.
Release the lock and record the time and the dummy's final position.
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting a slow tilt in a heavy dummy during the lock period, since a shifting load means the emergency lock does not hold under real weight.
ideal_interaction: Lift the dummy onto the pad with the dolly, turn the manual key switch to engage, and watch the tilt indicator until the timer runs out.
fit_note: Calibrate tunes a dial; the real test is physically moving a weighted load and checking a manual lock holds.

label: Submit fault list
human_steps: Gather the fault cards from each test station's clip tray.
Read each card's test step and fault code aloud.
Check each fault code against the test log on the console.
Type each confirmed fault into the form with its station name.
Mark critical faults in red at the top of the list.
Submit the list to the chief's inbox and wait for the receipt tone.
what_makes_it_hard: Typing fault codes exactly as printed on the cards, since one mistyped code sends the chief to the wrong station.
ideal_interaction: Type each fault code from its card into the form, then hold the submit key until the receipt tone and check the list count matches the cards in the tray.

label: Reactor and injector walk-round
human_steps: Walk the engineering corridor to the warp core and stop at the injector manifold railing
Read the temperature gauge on each of the four injector ports, saying each number aloud
Lay a hand flat on each constrictor housing to feel for unusual heat, then check the valve wheel is seated
Compare each trim setting on the panel against the last logged value on the clipboard
Write any drift in the log, initial it and note the time
Mistake: reading a stale gauge or logging the old trim value instead of the live one
what_makes_it_hard: Telling normal warm-up drift from a real trend, and the failure is logging a creeping drift as nominal.
ideal_interaction: Walk the warp core ring holding a handheld thermometer: sweep it across each of four injector ports in order, read the number, and turn the matching trim knob until the reading sits inside the green band; a missed port or an over-trim pushes the needle into red and flags the drift.
fit_note: Covers the valve element only; temperature reading, trim comparison and drift logging are missing.

label: Grid, gravity and life support rounds
human_steps: Walk the junction line from the first panel to the last, touching each cover plate to check it is latched
Open each breaker panel door and read the load meter on each breaker against the rated amperage stamped on its case
Lay the back of a finger on each breaker body to feel for heat, moving quickly to the next one
Read the plating load gauge and the scrubber status lamps at the end of the line
Reseat any tap connector that feels loose, using an insulated screwdriver, and retighten its terminal
Mistake: a breaker that reads under limit but is warm, which gets logged as fine
what_makes_it_hard: Judging heat and load together to spot a breaker about to trip, and the failure is a hot breaker missed until it trips under load.
ideal_interaction: Walk the junction line with the thermal probe in hand: press it to each breaker in turn, watch its load bar, and drag a warm breaker's slider back under its rated mark before the heat meter climbs; reseating a loose tap is a short hold-and-twist on its terminal.

label: Review work orders and assign crew
human_steps: Sit at the engineering desk and open the fault queue on the terminal
Read each ticket's system, location and symptom, noting any that touch life support, air or power
Rank the top ten tickets by risk and drag them into order
Check the crew roster board to see who is free and who has the right skills
Assign an ACE and a crew to each ticket and enter the expected finish time
Phone stores to chase any part not on the shelf and log the call
Mistake: sending a crew to a low-risk ticket while a life support fault waits
what_makes_it_hard: Ranking faults by real risk against crew availability, and the failure is an unsafe fault left waiting behind a cosmetic one.
ideal_interaction: Work the fault queue as a sorting game: drag each ticket by its risk tag (life, air, power, comfort) into the priority column, then drag a crew token onto the ticket; a life support ticket sitting below a comfort ticket costs a warning.

label: Engineering status to the XO
human_steps: Walk the four engineering stations and read the last value on each subsystem display
Write each reading on the status pad in one line: system, value, normal or not
Circle any reading outside its band and write the cause beside it
Pick the two items most likely to become a fault during the watch and mark them as worries
Pick up the comm handset, press the bridge channel and read the status line aloud
Mistake: sending the standard all-clear line without doing the walk, which the bridge later finds false
what_makes_it_hard: Summarising honestly means flagging a worry the bridge will not want to hear, and the failure is an all-clear built from memory.
ideal_interaction: Fill the status form only after pulling live readings: each of the four station readings must be opened and confirmed before its line can be submitted, and a line sent from an unopened reading is marked as an unverified report.
fit_note: The form can be filled without opening any live reading, so it does not require the walk that makes the report true.

label: Routine core and grid walk-round
human_steps: Carry a torch to the warp core and stand at the containment rail
Listen for the field hum and note any change in pitch against the last watch
Read the containment field strength dial and the injector temperature panel
Walk the grid junction line on the return, glancing at each breaker lamp for an amber flicker
Call the XO only if a reading has moved past its limit, otherwise log the watch as normal
Mistake: ignoring a shift in the hum because every dial still reads in range
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting a slow drift by ear and by comparing against earlier readings, and the failure is calling a creeping trend normal.
ideal_interaction: Walk the core ring with the torch: at each stop the field hum plays and the player holds the pitch dial on the reference note; a pitch that wanders gets a tick mark and a note in the watch log.

label: Clear one open work order with ACE
human_steps: Take the open work order off the board and walk to the engineering workbench
Fetch the replacement relay from the parts bin, checking its part code against the order
Remove the access panel with a spanner, setting its screws in a tray in order
Pull the faulty relay, note its scorch marking, and seat the new one
Connect the multimeter probes and check continuity and rated voltage across the relay
Refit the panel, sign the order and hand it back to ACE with the test result
Mistake: a screw left out that rattles in the panel later, or a crossed probe that reads a false pass
what_makes_it_hard: Working the repair in sequence without skipping the test, and the failure is a relay seated but never checked.
ideal_interaction: Use the spanner and multimeter on the open panel: turn each bolt in the order shown on screen, swap the relay by its code, then touch the probes to the terminals and hit the reading that matches the rated voltage.

label: Reserve power for sensor arrays
human_steps: Stand at the engineering power console and read the total budget bar
Check on the console's bridge order panel that the sensor allocation is approved
Set the sensor bus slider to the approved level, reading its number out loud
Watch the bus voltage meter for any dip below the rated line as the slider moves
Confirm the reserve bar still holds its safety margin for life support
Mistake: pushing the slider past the margin so the bus browns out during the survey
what_makes_it_hard: Granting sensor power without starving life support, and the failure is a brownout in the middle of the survey.
ideal_interaction: Drag the sensor bus slider up toward the approved line: the voltage meter must stay above its dip mark while the reserve bar keeps its safety margin, and overshooting the margin drops the bus.

label: Watch grid load during sweeps
human_steps: Stand at the junction monitor and read the grid load graph
Watch the load line through the sensor sweep, noting each rise
Call the bridge as soon as a spike crosses the warning mark, saying the value aloud
Shed one non-essential circuit by opening its breaker
Watch the load line settle back under the mark
Mistake: waiting too long so the spike trips a breaker in the middle of a scan
what_makes_it_hard: Acting on a rising trend before it trips the grid, and the failure is a breaker trip mid-scan.
ideal_interaction: Keep the grid load line under the warning mark as the sweep runs: when it climbs, tap the matching breaker to shed a circuit, and the player is scored on how fast the line falls back under the mark.

label: Check gravity plating and lifts for heavy loads
human_steps: Walk to the cargo lift and read the load rating plate on the cab wall
Inspect the cable and guide rails for fraying or grit, running a gloved hand along each
Check the brake pads through the inspection hatch with a torch
Send an empty test call, then a test pallet at the rated weight, watching the lift motor gauge
Listen for grinding on the ascent and note where the cab stops
Mistake: passing a lift that sticks under a loaded pallet because only the empty run was tested
what_makes_it_hard: Judging that a lift is safe at its rated load, not just empty, and the failure is a lift that sticks with a loaded pallet.
ideal_interaction: Run the lift up and down with a test weight in the cab: match the cab's load meter to the plate's rated mark and stop the lift within the target band; a grinding note on the motor gauge fails the check.

label: Hold steady power for transporter
human_steps: Stand at the engineering console and open the transporter buffer screen
Set the buffer to the target value the transporter chief calls over comm
Watch the capacitor bar fill, adjusting the input valve to keep the fill rate even
When the pattern lock light comes on, hold the buffer level and leave the input alone
Bleed off any surge with the bleeder valve before the bar reaches the top
Mistake: releasing the input during lock so the transport fails mid-cycle
what_makes_it_hard: Holding a level steady for a sustained window while the load shifts, and the failure is overcorrecting and dropping the lock.
ideal_interaction: Keep a steady hand on the input valve: hold the capacitor needle centred in its band while the pattern lock arrives, and bleed a surge by pressing the bleeder before the needle leaves the band.
fit_note: Calibrate is a one-off tuning to a set point; the real job is holding a level steady for a sustained window while the load changes.

label: Prioritise sickbay power and life support
human_steps: Open the power allocation board at the engineering console
Read the sickbay bus load and the biobed and scrubber draw figures
Ask the CMO over comm which systems are critical for the current patient list
Move the sickbay power slider up and the holding bus slider down, reading each change
Check the life support bus stays above its minimum after the change
Mistake: starving the scrubbers to power the biobeds, so sickbay air sags as patients arrive
what_makes_it_hard: Ordering power between medical and life support demands under time pressure, and the failure is sagging air or a biobed that drops out.
ideal_interaction: Shift power between the holding bus and the sickbay bus by dragging the two sliders; the biobed and scrubber gauges must both stay in their green band while the CMO's priority tag says which to protect first.

label: Confirm contamination isolation of ventilation
human_steps: Walk to the plant junction and find the isolation damper for the sickbay duct
Read the damper position indicator and confirm it reads fully closed
Hold the back of your hand at the nearest grille and feel for air moving through
Read the differential pressure manometer across the isolation damper
Confirm the negative pressure on the sickbay side and log the figure
Call the CMO with the reading and name any grille still moving air
Mistake: a damper that shows closed while air still moves through a grille
what_makes_it_hard: Trusting the air over the indicator, since a damper can read closed and still leak, and the failure is a contaminated shared duct.
ideal_interaction: Walk the duct line with the handheld airflow probe: sweep it across each grille and watch for a flow reading; turn the damper wheel closed until every grille reads zero and the manometer shows negative pressure.

label: Keep spare cells ready for sickbay
human_steps: Open the stores locker and carry the cell rack out to the bench
Press each cell into the cell tester and read its charge level
Move any cell under the set level onto the charging rack
Check the charge lamps on the rack and confirm each one lit
Label the rack with today's date and the sickbay tag
Mistake: returning a cell that tests low to the shelf with the full ones
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a cell that reads full from one that will hold under load, and the failure is a dead cell in a power cut.
ideal_interaction: Test the cells one by one at the bench: press each cell into the tester, watch its charge bar, and drop any bar under the mark into the charging slot; a cell that drains fast on the timer is pulled off the shelf.

label: Stage a controlled power-up test
human_steps: Walk to the warp core with the power-up checklist and confirm each step with the XO by comm
Bring the bus to standby at the first checkpoint and wait for the gauges to settle
Step the output up one notch at a time, holding at each checkpoint for its reading
Read injector temperature and field strength at every hold and compare them to the sheet
Stop the ramp at the first gauge over its limit and drop back one step
Mistake: skipping a hold so an untested limit is passed at full output
what_makes_it_hard: Holding at each checkpoint long enough for the gauges to settle, and the failure is an untested limit surfacing at full power.
ideal_interaction: Advance the output stepper one notch at a time: at each checkpoint the player holds the gauges steady for the timed hold, and a step taken before the hold ends or past a limit drops the test back to the last safe step.
fit_note: A generic power game does not enforce stepwise checkpoints with a timed hold at each stage.

label: Run systems drill with all crews
human_steps: Stand at the engineering console and read the drill scenario card aloud over comm
Phone each crew lead in turn and give them the scenario
Tick each crew's checklist items as they report done, noting who is slow
Start the stopwatch when the scenario is called and stop it when each crew confirms
Note any crew that misreports a step or skips a safety call
Mistake: ticking a step done before the crew has actually reported it
what_makes_it_hard: Judging each crew's response fairly by time and accuracy, and the failure is a fumbled step passed as done.
ideal_interaction: Run the drill on the console checklist: tap each crew's station when it reports, and the timer runs from the scenario call; an early tick before the crew's report is recorded as a false sign-off.

label: Write defect list for yard
human_steps: Collect the drill notes and the fault log from the desk
Go through each fault and copy its system, location and severity onto the yard form
Copy the tag number from the fault log onto each entry, checking the digits twice
Mark each defect as yard-fix or ship-fix in the disposition column
Read the finished list back against the fault log to check nothing was missed
Mistake: copying a serial number with two digits transposed, so the yard fixes the wrong part
what_makes_it_hard: Copying every defect with the right tag and severity, and the failure is an omitted or misnumbered fault that recurs next voyage.
ideal_interaction: Fill the yard form field by field from the fault log: each row is matched to its tag, and a wrong digit or a missing row is flagged on the form's check pass.

label: Pressure door and hatch rounds
human_steps: Take the seal gauge from its hook at the cargo bay door
Walk the deck hatches in sequence, checking each dogging handle is latched
Press the gauge's seal head against the gasket and read the pressure
Run a fingertip around the gasket for any draft or cold line
Tag any weeping gasket with a red tag and tighten the dog a quarter turn
Log each hatch in the repair queue with its tag number
Mistake: a gasket that reads fine on the gauge but leaks at one corner
what_makes_it_hard: Finding a slow leak by gauge and by feel together, and the failure is a weeping gasket left without a ticket.
ideal_interaction: Walk the hatch line with the gauge in hand: press the head to each gasket and hold until the needle settles, then drag a finger along the seal; a needle that drops or a cold draft spawns a red tag to clear.

label: Repair locker and breather audit
human_steps: Open the repair locker and pull the first tray forward
Count the patches, clamps and breathers by sliding fingers across each row
Check each extinguisher gauge needle sits in the green
Pull any short item from the stores cart and place it in its slot
Sign the inventory sheet with the count and the time
Mistake: counting a breather with a cracked seal as a full kit item
what_makes_it_hard: Counting exactly and noticing a damaged breather seal, and the failure is a broken kit item found only in an emergency.
ideal_interaction: Sort the locker trays by dragging each item into its slot; a breather with a cracked seal is caught by moving it into the inspection bin, and the count sheet must match the trays before it can be signed.

label: Fire suppression and valve test
human_steps: Phone engineering to say the suppression line is being tested
Walk to the junction and turn the first isolation valve wheel to close it
Connect the test gauge to the nozzle line and pump it up to test pressure
Hold the pressure for the timed interval, watching the needle for any drop
Check the foam level through the sight glass on the tank
Open the valve back up, reset the line and log the test
Mistake: signing a line green when the needle drifted during the hold
what_makes_it_hard: Holding pressure through the full interval and reading a small drop, and the failure is a jammed nozzle in a real fire.
ideal_interaction: Pump the test gauge up into the marked band and hold it there for the timer; a small drift on the needle shows as a leak, and the valve wheels must be turned in order before the foam level reads full.

label: Work the repair queue
human_steps: Pull the top ticket from the repair queue at the workbench
Pick a stock blank and fabricate the part on the press, checking its size with calipers
Carry the part and the repair kit to the site
Fit the part and tighten its bolts to the marked torque
Test the fit with a pressure or load check
Close the ticket on the terminal with the test result
Mistake: a plate cut a few millimetres short that looks right by eye but leaks
what_makes_it_hard: Cutting to the drawing size and checking it, and the failure is a part that looks right but fails under stress.
ideal_interaction: Cut the plate on the press: line the blank up to the drawing outline and feed it through; the calipers must read the marked size before the fit step unlocks, and a plate cut short is rejected at the test stage.

label: Routine seal and hatch rounds
human_steps: Walk the cargo deck quietly, listening at each hatch for a hiss
Look at each door's pressure indicator lamp for amber or red
Run a hand along the seal edge at the top and bottom corners
Try each latch lever and check it returns smoothly
Compare anything odd against the last watch log entry
Mistake: passing over a faint hiss at one corner because the indicator still shows green
what_makes_it_hard: Noticing a faint hiss or a stiff latch before a lamp changes, and the failure is a slow leak that grows unseen.
ideal_interaction: Walk the deck with the listening probe: approach each hatch and hold the probe at the seam, and a hiss tone rising above the baseline tags the door for a follow-up round.

label: Repair locker audit
human_steps: Pull the locker manifest sheet from its clip
Compare each printed line to the item count on the shelf
Mark each shortfall in pencil on the manifest
Pick up the missing items from the stores cart and place them in the locker
Initial each corrected line and return the manifest to its clip
Mistake: counting a patch from another locker tray to make a number match
what_makes_it_hard: Counting honestly against the printed quantity, and the failure is hiding a shortfall by borrowing from another tray.
ideal_interaction: Match each manifest line to its shelf: tap the shelf bin, count the items, and type the figure; a count that only matches after borrowing from another tray is flagged as a false tally.

label: Check hull plates and sensor mounts before maneuvers
human_steps: Suit up for outboard access and go through the hatch to the hull walkway
Tap each hull plate with a mallet, listening for a hollow sound
Put a torque wrench on the sensor mount bolts and check each reads spec
Grip each sensor mount and try to rock it by hand
Tag any loose or hollow plate and report it to the bridge
Mistake: missing a hollow plate because the tap was too light
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a sound plate from a hollow one by tap and feel, and the failure is a loose mount that rattles during a close pass.
ideal_interaction: Tap each hull plate on the grid with the mallet: a hollow tap rings a lower tone and must be marked, and each sensor mount gets a torque hold that must read inside its spec band.

label: Pre-stage patch kits near the lab
human_steps: Take a carry case from stores and go to the patch kit shelf
Load patch plates, clamps and sealant tubes into the case, sorted by size
Check each sealant tube's date stamp and set aside any expired
Carry the case to the lab and set it in the locker beside the door
Lock the locker and log the kit count with the time
Mistake: leaving an expired sealant tube in the case, where it gets grabbed in a hurry
what_makes_it_hard: Packing by size and checking every date, and the failure is an expired sealant tube grabbed during a debris strike.
ideal_interaction: Pack the case by dragging each kit item into its matching foam slot; a sealant tube whose date stamp has passed goes into the reject bin, and the case is staged only when every slot is full.

label: Inspect cargo bay seals and tie-downs
human_steps: Walk the cargo bay along the tie-down rail
Check each strap's tension by pulling it with a gloved hand
Look along the webbing for fraying, cuts or a stretched section
Run a fingertip along the bay door seal
Replace any frayed strap and retighten the rest with the ratchet
Mistake: accepting a strap that is slack at one end because the other end looks tight
what_makes_it_hard: Judging strap tension by feel and spotting webbing damage, and the failure is shifting cargo tearing a bulkhead panel.
ideal_interaction: Pull each strap on the tie-down rail: grab the strap and tug until its tension meter reads inside the band; a strap that drops under the mark or shows a frayed patch must be swapped before the bay is cleared.

label: Stand by with foam and clamps at loading
human_steps: Stand at the cargo locker with the foam extinguisher in hand
Scan the bay where crates are being lifted, watching for spills
Check the clamp set is lying ready and the hose is uncoiled
Call out any crate that swings or drops toward the bulkhead
Move in with the foam only when a spill starts, then stand back
Mistake: rushing into the lift path while the crate is still moving
what_makes_it_hard: Staying ready and watching without moving in too early, and the failure is a crush or spill with no fast response.
ideal_interaction: Hold the foam nozzle over the locker mark and watch the crate lane: the player waits, and a spill marker appearing in the lane is the cue to tap and sweep the foam across it, while stepping into the lane early costs points.
fit_note: A firecheck tests equipment; this job is standing ready and watching a live load, which the test does not mirror.

label: Patch scrapes after unload
human_steps: Walk the bay checking panels for scrapes and dents after the unload
Clean each scrape with the wire brush until bare metal shows
Cut a patch plate to fit the scrape and set it over the damage
Clamp the plate in place and tack weld each corner
Run a bead around the edge with the torch and let it cool
Mistake: welding too hot so the panel warps and the patch lifts
what_makes_it_hard: Controlling heat and fit while welding, and the failure is a warped panel or a patch that lifts.
ideal_interaction: Run the torch along the seam: keep the bead steady and the heat gauge in its band, and a bead that drifts past the mark or lingers on one spot warps the panel and fails the patch.

label: Seal-check sickbay isolation doors
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay isolation door and read the quarantine line marking on the deck
Press the gauge head to the door gasket and read the seal pressure
Check the isolation lamp on the door frame lights when the door is closed
Close and latch the door, then try the handle to make sure it holds
Mark the door as sealed on the log with the time
Mistake: marking a door sealed when the lamp was out and nobody checked the gasket
what_makes_it_hard: Confirming the seal with both gauge and lamp, and the failure is contamination crossing the quarantine line.
ideal_interaction: Close the sickbay door by turning the latch wheel: the seal gauge needle must rise into its band and the isolation lamp must light; a lamp that stays dark keeps the door flagged red.

label: Clear a corridor route for stretchers
human_steps: Walk the corridor and note every crate or box in the stretcher path
Measure the corridor width with the tape at its narrowest point
Carry each box into the side bay, lifting with the knees
Use the hand truck for the heavier crates
Walk the cleared route again and check it is at least one stretcher wide
Mistake: leaving a crate just inside the clearance line so a stretcher jams
what_makes_it_hard: Judging clearance precisely against the stretcher width, and the failure is a jammed transfer that slows the patient.
ideal_interaction: Clear the corridor by carrying crates one at a time into the side bay: drag each crate off the path, and the stretcher outline on the floor must stay clear of every crate before the route is marked open.

label: Run full hatch and bulkhead drill cycle
human_steps: Take the drill call from the bridge and start the stopwatch
Close each hatch in the cargo bay in order using its wheel handle
Dog each hatch and check the locking bar seats fully
Note any hatch that sticks, stalls or sounds wrong during the close
Open the cycle back to the start and log each hatch time
Mistake: closing a hatch without seating its bar, so the door looks shut but will not seal
what_makes_it_hard: Seating every locking bar fully inside the time target, and the failure is a stuck door found at the worst time.
ideal_interaction: Run the hatch cycle as a timed sequence: turn each wheel the right number of turns and watch its locking bar lamp turn green; a bar that does not seat before the timer ends is logged as a stuck door.

label: Test suppression and leak patching on mock breach
human_steps: Set up the mock breach with the test plate over the junction duct
Open the suppression line and run foam through the nozzle at the breach
Check the foam coverage by eye along the breach edge
Lay the sealant patch over the breach and press it down by hand
Clamp the patch and check it holds the test pressure on the gauge
Mistake: declaring the breach sealed when foam is leaking from one corner
what_makes_it_hard: Judging whether both foam and patch hold under pressure, and the failure is untested gear failing in a live breach.
ideal_interaction: Aim the foam nozzle at the breach plate and sweep until coverage fills the breach outline, then drag the patch onto the outline and hold the pressure gauge in band; a leak at any corner fails the test.
fit_note: A weld game covers only the patching step; the job also tests the suppression nozzle and foam coverage.

label: Fix defects found during shakedown
human_steps: Pull the defect list from the workbench terminal
Take each defect and find its part or tool in stores
Fit or fabricate the replacement at its site
Test the repaired item against its spec
Mark the defect closed on the list with the test result
Mistake: closing a defect without retesting the repaired item
what_makes_it_hard: Retesting each repair against spec before closing it, and the failure is a defect that stays on the ship.
ideal_interaction: Work the defect list from the top: take the matching part from the stores shelf, fit it at the site, and run the spec test before the entry can be closed; an entry closed before its test is returned to the list.

label: Life support sweep
human_steps: Pull the O2 and CO2 trend from the engineering terminal
Walk the junction and read each air quality sensor display
Hold your hand at each vent grille to check for airflow
Read the scrubber load gauge and note whether it is climbing
Reset the fan speed dial if a zone is under its target flow
Mistake: resetting a fan speed without checking the CO2 trend it was meant to fix
what_makes_it_hard: Reading a CO2 trend alongside the live sensors, and the failure is a slow CO2 climb that goes unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: Walk the junction with the air probe: sweep it past each vent while the CO2 readout on the terminal must stay in band; a rising reading brings up the fan dial, which you turn until the flow marker enters the target zone.

label: Coolant loop check
human_steps: Walk to the plant junction and read the pump pressure gauges
Compare each pressure against its band on the wall chart
Lay a palm on each heat exchanger housing to judge its temperature
Listen along the pipe runs for a hiss that suggests a steam leak
Tighten any weeping valve gland a quarter turn with the wrench
Mistake: missing a pressure drop because the gauge was read from the wrong side
what_makes_it_hard: Detecting a small pressure drop or a hiss before it becomes a steam leak, and the failure is a threat to reactor cooling.
ideal_interaction: Work the coolant line with the wrench: turn each gland until its pressure gauge sits in band, and a hiss tone on the pipe-run listener marks a leak that must be stopped before the loop passes.

label: Lighting controller sweep
human_steps: Open the lighting controller panel in the engineering junction
Scan the fault lights on the controller for any red or blinking zone
Pull a dead panel out of its frame and check its part number
Seat a replacement panel, pushing it until the latch clicks
Reset the flickering zone's breaker and watch the zone for a full minute
Mistake: resetting the breaker of a zone that was never flagged, leaving the real fault running
what_makes_it_hard: Matching a fault light to the right zone and panel, and the failure is a reset on the wrong zone while the fault stays live.
ideal_interaction: Fix the controller board: tap each red fault lamp to select its zone, drag the matching replacement panel into its frame, and the zone must hold steady for the timer before it is cleared.
fit_note: The breaker game covers the reset only; the job starts with fault scanning and panel swaps, which the game skips.

label: Hydroponics O2 balance
human_steps: Walk to the arboretum tree bank and read the O2 reclamation gauge
Compare the reading against the crew load figure on the board
Walk to the nutrient pumps and check each one with the botanist
Adjust the nutrient flow valve on the pump the botanist points to
Log the O2 reserve in the book and report it if it is below a third
Mistake: reporting a full reserve while the reclamation reading is falling
what_makes_it_hard: Judging the O2 reserve trend against crew load and nutrient flow, and the failure is a reserve that drops unseen.
ideal_interaction: Balance the O2 gauge against the load bar: turn the nutrient flow wheel so the reclamation needle stays above the crew load marker, and the reserve figure is logged only once the needle holds steady.

label: Full life support and coolant sweep
human_steps: Walk the full junction loop, starting with the air sensors
Read the CO2 level and scrubber load on each display
Walk to the coolant pump gauges and read each pressure
Feel the exchanger housings and listen along the lines for steam
Report any creeping CO2 or rising exchanger temperature to the ACE
Mistake: finishing the loop without noticing CO2 has crept up over three stops
what_makes_it_hard: Holding a slow trend across air and coolant readings at once, and the failure is a creep that stacks into a later fault.
ideal_interaction: Walk the junction loop with the sweep tablet: visit each air and coolant stop in order and note the CO2 and exchanger temperature at each one; a line that rises across three stops raises a flag.
fit_note: The valve game covers coolant valves only; the sweep also needs air quality, scrubber load and exchanger temperature trends.

label: Filter and panel maintenance
human_steps: Take a filter cartridge from the workbench and check its part code
Unscrew the vent panel and set the screws in a tray
Pull the old filter and hold it to the light to check for clogging
Slide the new filter in with its arrow pointing the way the air flows
Refit the panel and check it sits flush with no rattle
Mistake: fitting a filter backwards so the air bypasses it
what_makes_it_hard: Judging a clogged filter by light and fitting it the right way round, and the failure is a backwards filter that lets dust through.
ideal_interaction: Swap the filter: hold the old cartridge to the light and drag it out, then slot the new one with its arrow matching the airflow arrow; a backwards seat is flagged red and the panel will not close.

label: Hydro O2 reserve check
human_steps: Walk to the arboretum and read the reserve tank level gauge
Compare the reading with the last logged figure in the book
Note the rate of drop over the watch and write it beside the entry
Check the reclamation intake for blockage by looking at its screen
Report to the ACE if the reserve is falling faster than the rate limit
Mistake: copying the old reserve figure without reading the gauge
what_makes_it_hard: Reading a slow reserve drop against the log, and the failure is a reserve that drifts down unseen.
ideal_interaction: Read the reserve tank on screen: the player drags a level marker to the gauge's current level, and the drop rate is drawn from the log; a falling line steeper than the limit triggers the ACE call.

label: Raise air handling for extra lab and sensor load
human_steps: Walk to the lab console and read the current load figure
Read the lab air pressure and CO2 figures on the console screen
Turn the air handler fan dial up one step at a time
Listen for fan noise and check the lab's flow vent for draught
Ask the lab crew by comm whether the air feels stale, and adjust again if needed
Mistake: turning the fan up so far that the lab door seal is pulled open
what_makes_it_hard: Raising airflow enough for the load without overpressurising the room, and the failure is stale lab air or a pulled door seal.
ideal_interaction: Turn the air handler dial in small steps: the lab pressure needle and the CO2 readout must each enter their band, and pushing the dial past the pressure mark triggers a door-seal warning.

label: Check coolant for sensor array heat
human_steps: Walk to the plant junction and open the coolant trend chart
Read the array temperature from the sensor display
Watch the exchanger temperature line for a rise over the survey
Check the coolant flow gauge on the array feed
Report to the engineer if the array is heating faster than the chart allows
Mistake: calling the array cool based on one reading taken at the start
what_makes_it_hard: Reading a rising heat trend across the whole survey, and the failure is an array that throttles and loses scan quality.
ideal_interaction: Watch the coolant trend chart through the survey: the array temperature line must stay under its warning mark, and the player drags a flow slider up whenever the line climbs faster than its slope marker.

label: Balance hydro O2 against the longer sensor watch
human_steps: Walk to the arboretum tree bank and read the O2 reclamation gauge
Read the longer sensor watch's expected O2 draw from the board
Adjust the nutrient pump flow to match the draw, one pump at a time
Check the reserve tank level after each adjustment
Log the balance and the reserve figure before the watch ends
Mistake: balancing to the short-term load and leaving a low reserve for the long watch
what_makes_it_hard: Balancing reclamation against a longer demand than the current load, and the failure is a low reserve on the way home.
ideal_interaction: Balance the nutrient pumps against the sensor draw: drag each pump's flow slider until the O2 output marker matches the draw line, and the reserve must hold above its floor for the whole watch.

label: Ventilation check on cargo bay before loading
human_steps: Stand in the corridor at the cargo bay door and feel the vent grille
Read the cargo bay CO2 and humidity sensor on the wall panel
Check the fume extractor is running by listening to it and feeling its outlet
Read the sensors at each bay corner to look for stale pockets
Report any damp or fume reading to the ACE before loading starts
Mistake: giving a clear reading from the corridor while the far corner holds fumes
what_makes_it_hard: Checking the whole bay rather than the doorway, and the failure is fumes or damp goods in a stale corner.
ideal_interaction: Walk the cargo corridor with the probe: sweep it at the vent and at each of the four bay corners, and a corner reading over the fume mark gets flagged before the loading order is passed.

label: Watch temperature and humidity of stores
human_steps: Walk to the stores locker and read the hygrometer and thermometer
Check the perishables shelf for condensation or wilting
Adjust the locker's vent louvres to bring the humidity down
Read the temperature again after the louvres settle
Log the reading and tell the quartermaster if perishables are at risk
Mistake: leaving the louvres open so the stores heat up overnight
what_makes_it_hard: Holding humidity in band while the louvres shift conditions, and the failure is spoiled perishables.
ideal_interaction: Hold the locker climate by turning the louvre wheel: keep the humidity needle inside the green band while the temperature bar stays under its ceiling, and the perishables shelf shows wilting if either drifts too long.

label: Re-balance atmosphere after bay opens
human_steps: Walk to the engineering console and read the aft deck pressure figures
Check the cargo bay's differential pressure against the corridor
Turn the balance dial to bring bay pressure back to target
Read the aft deck CO2 level after each dial change
Confirm pressure and CO2 are both inside band before logging the balance
Mistake: balancing the bay on one reading while the aft CO2 climbs
what_makes_it_hard: Balancing pressure and CO2 across two zones at once, and the failure is a CO2 creep in the aft decks.
ideal_interaction: Balance the two zones on the console: turn the balance dial until the bay pressure marker lines up with the corridor, and the aft CO2 bar must stay in band through each turn; a dial change that drops the CO2 bar is rolled back.

label: Sickbay air filtration to isolation grade
human_steps: Walk to the nearest sickbay biobed and read the filter grade label
Check the filter's current setting on the sickbay wall panel
Turn the isolation dial to the isolation grade mark
Read the negative pressure gauge on the sickbay door to confirm the setting took
Report the grade to the CMO and log the time
Mistake: setting isolation grade without checking the door actually reads negative pressure
what_makes_it_hard: Confirming filtration grade by the gauge rather than the dial, and the failure is patients at infection risk.
ideal_interaction: Set the isolation dial on the sickbay panel: turn it to the grade mark and the negative pressure gauge must show a pull inside its band; the dial stays flagged until the gauge confirms it.

label: Extra scrubber capacity for crowded sickbay
human_steps: Walk to the engineering junction and check the scrubber bank status
Open the spare scrubber's access cover
Swap in the spare cartridge and tighten its retaining clamp
Bring the spare scrubber online and watch its load meter climb
Check the sickbay CO2 drops once the second unit runs
Mistake: bringing the spare online without seating the cartridge, so it runs without filtering
what_makes_it_hard: Seating the cartridge fully and confirming it is filtering, and the failure is a scrubber running unfiltered in a crowded ward.
ideal_interaction: Bring the spare scrubber online from the bank panel: drag the spare cartridge into its bay until it clicks, then the sickbay CO2 must fall below the ward marker; an unseated cartridge shows a no-filter warning.
fit_note: The dial sets a fan level only; the job is bringing a second scrubber unit online and seating its cartridge.

label: Verify water reclamation purity
human_steps: Walk to the plant junction and draw a water sample from the tap into a vial
Hold the sample against the light and check it is clear
Put a drop of the sample on the conductivity meter probe and read the figure
Compare the reading to the purity band on the chart
Log the sample with the time and tell the CMO if it fails
Mistake: reading the meter before the probe has settled, giving a falsely low number
what_makes_it_hard: Judging clarity by eye and conductivity by meter, and the failure is cloudy water that sickbay refuses to use.
ideal_interaction: Test the water sample: drop the vial's sample onto the meter probe, wait for the needle to settle, and the reading must fall in the purity band; a cloudy sample is flagged before the meter is read.

label: Cycle every environmental subsystem under load
human_steps: Start at the engineering junction with the test checklist
Switch on the scrubbers, fans and pumps in order, one at a time
Read each subsystem's indicator after its switch-on and note its load
Bring up the lights in each zone and confirm the zone lamp
Shut each subsystem down in reverse and check its shutdown lamp
Mistake: switching a pump on before its isolation valve is open, so it runs dry
what_makes_it_hard: Sequencing every subsystem under load without a dry-run, and the failure is a weak link hidden until real trouble.
ideal_interaction: Run the subsystem cycle at the console: flip each switch in checklist order, and a pump switched on before its valve shows a dry-run warning; each indicator must turn green before the next subsystem can start.
fit_note: A power game allocates energy; the job is sequencing switch-ons and shutdowns with indicator checks and valve order.

label: Test emergency atmosphere isolation and lights
human_steps: Walk to the junction and trigger the emergency isolation switch
Watch each damper's position lamp to confirm it has closed
Listen for the zone fans cutting out
Trip the emergency light circuit and check each lamp lights on battery
Reset the isolation and restore the lights, checking each zone lamp
Mistake: calling the isolation a pass when one damper lamp stayed amber
what_makes_it_hard: Checking every damper and lamp rather than the first one, and the failure is a drill that fails and gets noted by the bridge.
ideal_interaction: Throw the isolation switch and walk the damper row: each lamp must turn from amber to red and the emergency lights must come on in every zone; a single amber lamp fails the test.
fit_note: The dial game turns a single value; the job is a sequence of isolation switches, damper lamp checks and light tests across zones.

label: Post-test report with fault list
human_steps: Collect the test log and the fault tickets from the engineering desk
Go through each subsystem's result and note its faults in the log
Write each fault on the list with its system, location and severity
Add the ticket number to each fault and check it matches the ticket
Sign the report and send it to the ACE
Mistake: leaving out a fault that was fixed on the spot but never logged
what_makes_it_hard: Capturing every fault from the test with the right severity, and the failure is faults forgotten so the debt carries over.
ideal_interaction: Fill the post-test form from the test log: each subsystem result is copied row by row, and a fault fixed on the spot still needs its row, which the form flags as missing if left out.

label: Charge-rack round
human_steps: Take the cell-gauge handset from its hook at the armory junction and walk the charger racks, starting at the left-hand rack.
Press the gauge probe onto each cell's contact plate and read the dial, noting any cell reading under 80 percent.
Pull a sagging cell from its cradle with both hands and check the cradle latch clicks open.
Seat a full cell from the shelf and confirm its charge lamp turns steady green rather than blinking amber.
Wipe a grey film off a contact plate with the dry cloth before reseating the cell.
Write each rack's levels on the clipboard sheet and tick the rack number when done.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading true charge from a contact-only dial and spotting a cradle that is not seating; a weak cell sent out means weapons that fail when an alert arrives.
ideal_interaction: Carry the gauge handset down the rack aisle, touch its probe to each cell in turn, and swap any cell whose needle drops under the amber line for a fresh one, pressing it into the cradle until the lamp steadies green.

label: Serial-number audit
human_steps: Open the zapper locker and take the issue ledger from the shelf beside it.
Lift each zapper from its clip and read the stamped serial on the grip with the torch held close.
Find the matching ledger line and tick it with a pencil only when every digit agrees.
On a mismatch, check the sign-out slip for that serial and note who held it last.
Count the power-cell slots against the cell count written on the ledger's front page.
Relock the locker, pull the seal strip across the door and initial it.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading worn stamped serials digit by digit and refusing a near-match tick; a wrong tick hides a missing weapon.
ideal_interaction: Take each zapper off its clip, hold the grip under the torch, and match its serial digit by digit against the ledger, ticking only exact matches and stopping to chase any digit that differs.

label: Force-field emitter test
human_steps: Carry the emitter tester from the armory to the brig corridor and step over the threshold strip.
Stand at the first emitter housing and press the probe to its grille, holding for a three-second reading.
Listen for the emitter hum and watch the bar graph for a dip under the lower mark.
Repeat at each housing along the corridor, logging the housing number and its reading in order.
Hang a weak-tag on any emitter under the mark and note its position on the corridor plan.
Report the weak emitter number to the Deputy from the corridor panel.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a weakening field from a noisy one within three seconds per reading; a missed weak emitter lets an intruder or patient pass a dead field.
ideal_interaction: Walk the brig corridor with the tester, pressing the probe to each emitter grille and holding until the bar graph settles; tag any emitter whose bar stays under the lower mark, and re-read the ones that flicker.

label: Issue and returns desk
human_steps: Stand at the desk and swipe the requester's badge through the reader, checking the name on the screen.
Compare the authority signature on the request slip with the Deputy's standing list.
Lift the requested weapon from the rack, checking its charge lamp and seal tag.
Hand over the gear and have the holder sign the out-log with the time written beside the signature.
Rotate a returned zapper under the inspection lamp, looking down the barrel for scoring and the grip for fouling.
Enter the return time and condition code, and send any dirty gear to the workbench.
what_makes_it_hard: Refusing an unsigned request while the requester pushes; a weapon issued without authority is the failure the Deputy will ask about.
ideal_interaction: Scan the requester's badge, match the request slip against the standing list, and refuse the hand-over if the signature line is blank; on return, rotate each zapper under the inspection lamp and log its condition before filing it.
fit_note: Badge covers the authority check only; the return inspection under the lamp and the charge-lamp check are not represented.

label: Full charger round and top up all cells
human_steps: Walk the charger aisle with the cell caddy and check each rack's power lamp from the doorway.
Pull every cell from the racks in rack order and lay them on the caddy tray by rack number.
Check each cell's terminals for scorch marks and wipe them with the contact cloth.
Seat the cells back, topping up the lowest reading first, and wait for the charge tone.
Set a spare on the bench charger and write its starting level on the tag.
Log the full-round time on the rack board and sign the sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Knowing a cell is truly full rather than sitting on trickle charge; failure leaves weapons weak when an alert comes.
ideal_interaction: Lift each cell from its rack onto the caddy tray, wipe its terminals and reseat it, then hold it on the bench charger until the full tone sounds, topping up the lowest cells first.

label: Serial audit of the zapper locker
human_steps: Open the zapper locker and count the clips on the rail from left to right.
Lift each zapper and read its serial off the grip.
Compare each serial against the ledger page and tick its line.
Note any serial with no ledger line and check the sign-out slips for it.
Close the locker and place the seal.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a missing weapon from one signed out elsewhere; failure is a missing weapon going unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: Walk the zapper rail, lifting each weapon to read its grip serial and ticking it on the ledger, and chase any serial that has no matching line.
fit_note: A manifest tick list does not require reading each weapon's serial from the grip.

label: Issue sidearms and trackers to the landing party
human_steps: Read the landing-party roster on the desk screen and call each name in turn.
Pull a sidearm and a tracker from the rack for each person, checking the tracker battery lamp.
Turn the tracker's channel dial until the away-channel lamp shows steady.
Hand each item over and have the person sign the roster beside their name.
Count the empty rack slots against the roster and note the gap on the sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Matching each person to the right gear in order without skipping one; failure is an away team going down unarmed or untracked.
ideal_interaction: Take a sidearm and tracker from the rack for each name on the roster, dial the tracker to the away channel until its lamp is steady, then hand both over only after the signature is written.
fit_note: Badge covers the sign-out only; the tracker channel dial and battery lamp checks are not represented.

label: Check the force-field emitters at the transporter
human_steps: Walk to the transporter pad with the emitter tester and step into the pad's inner ring.
Hold the probe to each emitter housing on the four posts, one at a time.
Read the bar graph and log each post's reading in clockwise order.
Run the tester along the door seal and look for any gap wider than a finger's width.
Step off the pad and toggle the pad field to standby to test the return reading.
Log the pad reading and lock the emitter cabinet.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging whether a seal gap is wide enough to fail containment; failure is a contaminant or intruder passing the pad.
ideal_interaction: Walk the pad's four posts holding the probe to each housing, then sweep the tester along the door seal and log any post that reads low or any seal gap.

label: Receive and clean gear on return
human_steps: Take the returned gear from the intake tray and lay each weapon on the bench mat.
Strip the grip cover and remove the power cell, checking the cell terminals for residue.
Wipe the barrel with a dry patch first, then a solvent patch, in one pass from breech to muzzle.
Brush the emitter port clean and check it with the torch for grit.
Reassemble and press the grip cover home until it clicks, then fit a fresh cell.
Shelve the cleaned weapon and tag its return slip.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging when a weapon is clean enough to store; failure is fouled gear locked up dirty and jamming when it is needed.
ideal_interaction: Strip each returned zapper on the bench mat, wipe the barrel in one breech-to-muzzle pass with the solvent patch, then reassemble until the grip cover clicks home.

label: Inspect and seal cargo-bay hazard lockers
human_steps: Walk into the cargo bay with the seal tape roll and the hazard log.
Read the hazard label on each locker front against the cargo manifest.
Open the locker and check its pressure gauge against the green band.
Close the lid and press the latch until it drops with a clear click.
Run seal tape along the lid seam, pressing it flat with the palm as you go.
Sign the seal tag and log the locker number and seal time.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading a gauge against its band and refusing to seal a leaking lid; failure is dangerous cargo sitting unsecured.
ideal_interaction: Open each hazard locker and read its gauge, running the seal tape along the lid seam only when the needle sits in the green band, pressing it flat with the palm.

label: Issue escort weapons for the handoff
human_steps: Check the handoff order on the desk screen and note the number of escorts.
Pull each escort zapper from the rack and read its serial against the order sheet.
Check each weapon's charge lamp and fit its safety pin in place.
Scan the escort's badge against the handoff order before the hand-over.
Hand the weapon and its tag across the desk and watch the escort clip it to the belt.
Enter the issue time and escort names in the out-log.
what_makes_it_hard: Matching each weapon to the right escort and refusing an unsigned order; failure is a cargo handoff with no armed escort.
ideal_interaction: Pull each escort zapper from the rack, check its charge lamp and fit its safety pin, then hand it across the desk only after the escort's badge matches the handoff order.
fit_note: Badge covers the order check; the charge-lamp and safety-pin checks at hand-over are not represented.

label: Reconcile returns after the handoff
human_steps: Pull the out-log and count the lines marked issued.
Walk to the returns rack and count each weapon by touching it.
Match each returned serial to its out-log line and cross that line off.
Chase any weapon logged out but missing from the rack, checking the handoff slips.
Write the net count at the foot of the log and sign it.
Hand the reconciled log to the shift officer.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping the count honest when a weapon is still out; failure is a wrong gear count at shift change.
ideal_interaction: Count the returns rack by touching each weapon in turn, crossing its serial off the out-log, and chasing any logged weapon with no return until the two counts agree.
fit_note: Reads a manifest list; no physical count of the returns rack is performed.

label: Prepare quarantine-escort kits and restraints
human_steps: Open the escort locker and pull a blank kit case from the bottom shelf.
Click each restraint through its ratchet to the first stop and back, checking it locks.
Pack the restraint pair, gloves and seal tags into the case in the order on the kit card.
Press the case latch until it clicks shut and test it with a tug.
Write the kit number and date on a tag and clip it to the handle.
Shelve the kit on the front rack with its tag facing out.
what_makes_it_hard: Confirming each restraint actually locks and the kit is complete before it leaves; failure is security unable to enforce a ward cordon.
ideal_interaction: Pack each kit from its card, click each restraint through its ratchet to confirm it locks, then latch the case and clip a numbered tag to its handle.

label: Test brig and sickbay door force-fields
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay door and stand at the control plate holding the field tester.
Press the tester's sensor to the door frame at hip height, then at shoulder height.
Watch the field indicator for steady amber rather than a flicker, and listen for the buzz.
Pass a hand through the doorway to confirm the field pushes it back.
Log the reading and the time on the door card.
Report any door with a dim lamp to the Deputy.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading a field that flickers rather than fails outright; failure is patients or contacts wandering out of the ward.
ideal_interaction: Hold the tester's sensor to the sickbay door frame at hip and shoulder height, then pass a hand through the doorway to see the field resist it, logging any corner where the indicator dips.

label: Run a full weapons and emitter test
human_steps: Clamp the first zapper into the bench test rig and connect the lead to its power port.
Fire one low-setting shot into the target block and read the meter.
Repeat at medium and high settings, logging each meter reading.
Move the emitter tester to the bench and run a field check on the bench emitter.
Compare each reading with the spec card and pull any weapon outside the band.
Sign the weapon's test card and hang it in the rack.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging output against spec across several settings; failure is faults that only surface in a real emergency.
ideal_interaction: Clamp each zapper into the bench rig, fire at low, medium and high settings into the target block, and pull any weapon whose meter reading drops out of the spec band.

label: Live-fire calibration at the range
human_steps: Carry the zapper to the range line and set the target at the twenty-metre marker.
Brace the weapon on the bench rest and align the front and rear sights on the target centre.
Fire a three-shot group and mark each impact on the target card.
Measure the group's offset from centre with the ruler.
Turn the elevation screw a quarter turn with the spanner to shift the group toward centre.
Fire a second group to confirm the zero holds, then clip the card.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading small offsets on a three-shot group and adjusting by the right amount; failure is zappers drifting off zero.
ideal_interaction: Brace the zapper on the bench rest, fire a three-shot group, measure its offset with the ruler, and turn the elevation screw with the spanner until a second group lands in the centre ring.
fit_note: Bench-test kind; live aiming, group measurement and zero-screw adjustment at the range are not represented.

label: Report all findings to the Deputy
human_steps: Open the readiness form on the armory console and read the blank fields.
Enter the weapon count from the rack and the number of test cards filed.
Enter each cell's lowest reading and each emitter's reading from the logs.
Attach the bench results and mark any item below spec in the red box.
Re-read the form line by line against the logs before sending.
Press send and wait for the Deputy's receipt tone.
what_makes_it_hard: Making every number traceable to a log entry rather than a memory; failure is the bridge flying blind on defensive readiness.
ideal_interaction: Fill the readiness form field by field from the logs, checking each number against its source card before pressing send and waiting for the receipt tone.

label: Junction and tap inspection round
human_steps: Pick up the tricorder from its charging cradle and check the battery bar.
Walk to the engineering junction and find the access panel by its yellow edge.
Unlatch the panel with a quarter-turn on the key and swing it open.
Sweep the tricorder over each tap in turn and read the load percentage.
Press reset on any breaker that has tripped once and count the trips in the junction book.
Close and latch the panel, then log the round.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding the tricorder at each tap long enough for a true load reading and recognising a tap that trips again; failure is a marginal tap drifting into a blackout.
ideal_interaction: Walk the junction with the tricorder, sweeping it over each tap and noting its load percentage, then reset a tripped breaker only once and log every trip.

label: Balance grid load against reactor output
human_steps: Stand at the engineering console and read the load bar for each grid section.
Note the hottest conduit, the section running above 80 percent.
Walk to the console shelf and find the reactor output figure for this shift on the spec sheet.
Drag the lighting and lift sliders off the hot conduit onto cooler sections.
Watch the readout settle for ten seconds before trusting it.
Write the grid figure and the spec figure on the load sheet and initial it.
what_makes_it_hard: Moving several sections at once so no conduit crosses its limit while the output figure changes; failure is a rolling tap.
ideal_interaction: Drag loads from the hottest conduit onto cooler sections on the grid screen, holding each shift until the readout stops moving, and keep every section under the limit line.

label: Replace worn power taps
human_steps: Walk to the spares locker and pull a matching tap from the foam tray, checking its part number.
Carry the spare and a tap wrench back to the workbench.
Close the feed valve and check that the feed lamp goes dark.
Unbolt the worn tap's four retaining bolts and lift it out.
Seat the spare and tighten its bolts in a cross pattern.
Reopen the feed valve and watch the load lamp settle.
what_makes_it_hard: Isolating the conduit properly and tightening bolts evenly; failure is a live arc or a loose tap.
ideal_interaction: Close the feed valve, unbolt the worn tap with the wrench, seat the spare and tighten its four bolts in a cross pattern before reopening the valve and watching the load lamp.

label: Routine junction round
