human_steps: Walk to the engineering junction carrying only the torch.
Read each breaker's switch position and check its lamp colour.
Press the back of your hand to each breaker casing to feel for heat.
Note any casing that feels warm and any switch sitting halfway.
Leave the breakers untouched and log the state in the junction book.
Walk back and drop the book on the console.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a warm breaker from a normal one by touch alone; failure is marginal taps drifting until they trip mid-shift.
ideal_interaction: Walk the junction with the torch, pressing the back of your hand to each breaker casing in turn and logging any that feel warm or sit halfway between positions.

label: Update load sheet
human_steps: Pull the load sheet from the clip beside the console.
Read the grid total from the top readout and write it in the first box.
Copy each section's percentage from the sections panel, one section at a time.
Work out each section's margin to the ninety percent line and write it in the margin column.
Add the section figures and check they match the grid total.
Sign the sheet and clip it back.
what_makes_it_hard: Copying many figures into the right rows and catching a sum that does not add up; failure is the next shift working blind.
ideal_interaction: Transcribe each section's percentage from the sections panel into its matching sheet row, then check that the rows sum to the grid total before the sheet is accepted.

label: Route extra power to science arrays
human_steps: Walk to the lab junction and read the bridge order slip pinned beside the panel.
Open the junction panel and find the array feed bus by its colour band.
Check the array bus voltage with the meter before touching anything.
Throw the bus switch from main to array feed in small steps.
Watch the array voltage climb and the main bus gauge hold steady.
Log the reroute and the bridge order number on the panel card.
what_makes_it_hard: Feeding the arrays enough without dropping the main bus; failure is arrays browning out and scans failing.
ideal_interaction: Read the order slip, check the array bus with the meter, and throw the bus switch over in small steps while the main bus gauge stays inside its band.
fit_note: Screen-based power game; the real reroute is a physical bus switch at the lab junction, checked against a bridge order.

label: Watch tap load during long scans
human_steps: Sit at the console and open the tap load trend graph for the scan.
Follow each tap's line across the graph, noting any climb toward the upper mark.
Mark the time when a tap's line bends upward and keeps rising.
Shed a non-essential load section before the line crosses the upper mark.
Keep the trend on screen until the scan ends and mark each dip.
Enter the peak load value in the scan log.
what_makes_it_hard: Catching a slow climb early enough to shed before a trip; failure is an overloaded conduit tripping mid-scan.
ideal_interaction: Follow each tap's trend line through the scan, and shed load on any section whose line bends upward toward the upper mark before it crosses.

label: Power the cargo lifts and tractor gear
human_steps: Walk to the cargo junction and read the lift and tractor feed labels on the panel.
Open the junction cover and find the lift feed breaker and the tractor coil breaker.
Switch the lift feed on and listen for a clean idle with no grinding.
Press the tractor coil test button and check its warm-up lamp.
Set the tractor feed to the level the cargo placard gives for this load.
Close the cover and log the feed setting and the placard number.
what_makes_it_hard: Matching feed to the load rating so the lifts do not stall; failure is lifts stalling with a load on.
ideal_interaction: At the cargo junction panel, switch on the lift feed, listen for a clean idle, then set the tractor feed to the placard level for the load while the test button confirms the coil lamp.
fit_note: Screen-based power game; the real work is physical breaker and feed setting at the cargo junction against a placard.

label: Check transporter pad feed
human_steps: Walk to the transporter junction and read the pad feed label on the panel.
Open the panel and check the pad breaker is fully on, not halfway.
Press the pad test button and watch the pad lamp turn from red to green.
Run the back of your hand along the pad feed cable to feel for heat along its length.
Close the panel and write the pad reading in the transporter book.
Confirm the feed to the transporter chief over the intercom.
what_makes_it_hard: Checking the feed holds under load, not just that the lamp is lit; failure is a delayed beam-down.
ideal_interaction: Press the pad test button and hold the breaker against its stop while the pad lamp must turn green and stay green, then run a heat check along the feed cable.

label: Prioritise sickbay power
human_steps: Walk into sickbay and find the junction box behind the biobed rail.
Read the priority labels and find the biobed feed at the top of the stack.
Set the biobed feed to priority one and the lights to priority three.
Watch each biobed indicator for a flicker over a ten-second count.
Count the active biobeds against the priority ladder.
Log the priority setting on the sickbay card and tell the nurse by name.
what_makes_it_hard: Ordering feeds by patient risk without starving a bed; failure is biobeds flickering during treatment.
ideal_interaction: Set the priority switches on the sickbay junction so each biobed feed sits above the lights, then watch every biobed lamp for a flicker over a full ten-second count.
fit_note: Screen-based power game; the real priority is set by physical switches in the sickbay junction box, checked against biobed lamps.

label: Add backup tap for sickbay
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay junction and fetch a backup tap and two jumper leads from the kit case.
Open the junction box and identify the live feed and the empty tap socket.
Strip the lead ends and seat them into the tap's terminals.
Fit the backup tap into the empty socket and tighten its clamp.
Route the jumper lead along the cable tray, clipping it at each hook.
Cut the main feed and confirm the backup lamp holds.
what_makes_it_hard: Making a sound connection with the right polarity in a crowded box; failure is a single trip cutting all treatment.
ideal_interaction: Connect the jumper lead from the live feed to the backup tap by dragging each wire end into its matching colour socket, clip it along the tray, then confirm the lamp holds when the main feed is cut.

label: Stress-test grid under high load
human_steps: Walk to the engineering console and open the load bank panel.
Switch on the load bank in ten-percent steps, starting from zero.
At each step, read the tap temperatures and the breaker lamps.
Hold each step for a ten-second count and note any lamp that starts to flicker.
Stop the test at the first tap that goes hot or trips, and record the load.
Shed the load bank back to zero and log the breaking point.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding each step long enough to see a slow warm-up and stopping before a trip; failure is weak junctions failing in the real drill.
ideal_interaction: Raise the load bank in ten-percent steps on the console, pausing at each for a ten-second count and stopping the moment a tap reads hot or a breaker lamp flickers.

label: Replace taps found hot
human_steps: Take the tap flagged hot in the stress test from the cool-down tray at the bench.
Inspect its contacts under the bench lamp for pitting or blackening.
Fetch a replacement from the spares locker and check its rating label.
Close the feed valve and unclip the old tap.
Seat the new tap and tighten its terminal screws with the torque driver to the click.
Reopen the feed and feel the new tap's casing after five minutes for heat.
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting pitted contacts that caused the heat rather than refitting a bad part; failure is faults carrying into the next phase.
ideal_interaction: Inspect the flagged tap's contacts under the bench lamp, replace it with one from the locker, and tighten the terminals with the torque driver to the marked click before restoring the feed.

label: Report junction margins
human_steps: Open the margin report form on the console and read its header.
Enter each junction's load figure from the load sheet.
Work out each junction's headroom to the ninety percent line and enter it.
Mark any junction with under ten percent headroom in the flag box.
Re-check each figure against the load sheet, line by line.
Send the form to the bridge and wait for the receipt.
what_makes_it_hard: Computing headroom correctly per junction and flagging the weak ones; failure is the bridge unaware of weak points.
ideal_interaction: Fill the margin form field by field from the load sheet, subtracting each junction's load from its ninety percent line and flagging any under ten percent before sending to the bridge.

label: Core temperature and injector rounds
human_steps: Walk to the warp core and stand on the grated platform at the lower rail.
Read the plasma temperature gauge on the left column and note the figure.
Sight along each injector nozzle to check its alignment against the painted line.
Lean in and listen beside each injector for a harmonic hum, noting any whine.
Touch the cooling housing with the back of a hand for heat.
Log the temperatures and alignment on the core sheet and sign it.
what_makes_it_hard: Hearing a harmonic change and judging a slight misalignment by eye; failure is an injector fault that starves the core.
ideal_interaction: Walk the core platform, sighting each injector nozzle for alignment and leaning in to listen for a harmonic whine, logging any injector that drifts from its line.

label: Constrictor and output trim
human_steps: Open the reactor console and read the output figure against the EPS demand.
Note the gap and decide whether the constrictors must add or shed output.
Turn the constrictor trim dial one notch at a time.
Wait for the output needle to settle through a full count before the next notch.
Stop when output sits in the demand band and watch it for stability.
Record the final trim notch and output on the trim sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Trimming in small steps and waiting for the needle to settle; failure is output oscillating or overshooting demand.
ideal_interaction: Turn the constrictor trim dial one notch at a time, waiting for the output needle to settle before each next notch, until it sits in the demand band.

label: Coolant loop cross-check
human_steps: Walk to the coolant junction and read the flow gauge on the manifold.
Compare that flow figure with the core temperature you logged at the core.
Check the manifold pipe for a sweat line or a frost mark.
Place a hand flat on the outlet pipe and feel for a temperature change along its length.
Note the drift if the flow is more than ten percent below normal.
Write the coolant reading beside the core temperature and report any drift to the bridge.
what_makes_it_hard: Seeing that flow and core numbers disagree before the core runs hot; failure is coolant drift becoming a fault.
ideal_interaction: Read the manifold flow gauge, check the outlet pipe for a frost mark, then compare the flow figure against the core temperature to note any drift.
fit_note: Valve-turning activity; the real cross-check is reading the flow gauge and comparing it with core temperature, with no valve action.

label: Baseline core log
human_steps: Sit at the reactor console and open the core log for the last shift.
Scroll to the first steady entry and note its plasma temperature and output as baseline.
Scan down the log and mark each entry where temperature drifts more than two degrees from baseline.
Check the injector and coolant columns for matching drift.
Copy the baseline figures onto the shift handover card.
Sign the handover with the time.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a real drift from a one-off spike in noisy log data; failure is drift going unnoticed until it becomes a fault.
ideal_interaction: Trace the core log's temperature trend from the first steady entry, marking each point that drifts more than two degrees from baseline.

label: Injector wear survey
human_steps: Walk to the warp core with the wear gauge and a torch.
Remove the cover plate over the first injector and shine the torch into the nozzle.
Look at the nozzle lip for a pale ring or glaze, the early wear mark.
Seat the wear gauge pins one at a time in the nozzle bore, noting any pin that will not go in.
Repeat for each injector, moving clockwise round the core.
Refit each cover plate firmly and log the wear reading.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging a wear mark from a pale ring by torchlight and measuring bore size, not lip size; failure is a worn injector failing later.
ideal_interaction: Remove each injector's cover plate, shine the torch into the nozzle and seat the wear gauge pins one at a time in the bore, logging any pin that will not go in.

label: Raise sensor array power budget
human_steps: Open the power budget panel at the reactor console.
Read the current sensor budget and the total output headroom.
Raise the sensor budget one step at a time on the slider.
Watch the headroom figure after each step and keep it above the margin.
Stop at the last step that keeps the margin, and back off one step if it dips.
Log the new sensor budget and headroom on the budget sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Finding the largest sensor budget that keeps headroom above the line; failure is sensors browning out mid-scan.
ideal_interaction: Drag the sensor budget slider up in steps on the budget panel, stopping at the last step where the headroom figure stays above the margin line.

label: Hold steady output during scan
human_steps: Walk to the warp core and place your hand on the output lever.
Read the output needle and the scan demand line on the warpcore panel.
Hold the lever at its notch, feeling for any drift in its resistance.
Make small corrections the moment the needle wanders off the band.
Keep the hold through the scan countdown without letting go.
Release the lever to neutral and log the scan's peak and minimum output.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding the lever steady for the full scan with tiny corrections; failure is fluctuation ruining the scan data.
ideal_interaction: Hold the output lever at the warpcore panel's notch with a steady press, making tiny corrections whenever the needle drifts, until the countdown ends and you release to neutral.
fit_note: Screen-based power game; the real work is a sustained manual hold on the output lever at the warp core, with no hold-and-release.

label: Prep for transport/lift load surge
human_steps: Open the surge panel at the reactor console and read the expected lift draw.
Check the reserve bar and confirm it covers the draw.
Pre-raise the output trim one step so the reserve is topped before the surge.
Set the surge limiter to the draw figure and lock it.
Fire the test pulse and watch the output needle through it.
Log the reserve figure and the limiter setting.
what_makes_it_hard: Pre-loading enough reserve for a sudden draw without overheating; failure is the transporter draw sagging.
ideal_interaction: Set the surge limiter to the expected draw on the panel, pre-raise the output trim one step, then fire the test pulse and watch the reserve bar stay above its floor.

label: Trim to cruise efficiency
human_steps: Open the cruise curve on the console and read the current output point.
Find the point on the curve where it flattens.
Lower the output trim toward the cruise figure in steps.
Check the fuel-draw readout after each step to confirm it falls.
Stop where fuel draw is lowest and output still meets demand.
Log the cruise setting and fuel figure on the cruise card.
what_makes_it_hard: Finding the flat part of the efficiency curve without starving demand; failure is wasted fuel and extra heat.
ideal_interaction: Trace the cruise curve on the console, lowering the output trim until the fuel readout stops falling, and stop at the last point above demand.

label: Maximise burst output for speed
human_steps: Open the burst panel at the reactor console and read the temperature margin.
Confirm with the bridge that burst is ordered and note the time.
Hold the burst key until the output needle begins to move.
Watch the core temperature line, not the output, for any rise.
Ease the burst back the moment the temperature reaches the margin line.
Log the burst duration and peak temperature on the burst card.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding burst while watching temperature rather than the output that looks good; failure is core overheating.
ideal_interaction: Hold the burst key on the reactor console while watching the temperature line, easing off the instant the line crosses the margin mark.
fit_note: Screen-based power game; the real burst is a timed hold guided by the temperature line, with no temperature-linked release.

label: Watch core temps at high output
human_steps: Walk to the warp core and station yourself at the temperature gauge rail.
Read the plasma temperature every ten seconds and call the figure aloud.
Touch the cooling housing with the back of a hand on each count.
Check the frost line on the coolant pipe for any change.
Note the moment the temperature climbs past the warning tick.
Call the bridge with the peak figure once output drops.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping a steady count of readings under load and noticing a climb early; failure is core overheating.
ideal_interaction: Stand at the core's temperature rail, reading the gauge on each ten-second count and touching the housing, and call out the moment the reading passes the warning tick.
fit_note: Trend graph; the real work is physically watching the core gauge and housing at the warp core.

label: Prioritise sickbay power
human_steps: Open the sickbay feed panel at the reactor console.
Confirm the sickbay priority request on the bridge order screen.
Raise the sickbay feed share on the priority slider.
Take the difference from the lowest-priority share so the total stays under output.
Check the biobed grid on the console for steady green lamps.
Log the new shares and the time on the priority card.
what_makes_it_hard: Redistributing a fixed output so sickbay gets its share without starving life support; failure is biobeds flickering.
ideal_interaction: Drag the sickbay share slider up on the priority panel and take the difference from the lowest-priority share, keeping the total under the output line while the biobed grid stays green.

label: Run injector stress test
human_steps: Walk to the warp core and clip the stress lead onto the first injector.
Turn the stress dial to its first setting and hold for the count.
Listen for a harmonic whine and watch the nozzle glow through the sight port.
Step the dial up one setting and repeat for each injector.
Pull the lead the moment the glow goes uneven or the whine rises.
Log the top setting each injector held and how it failed.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging a whine and an uneven glow as the injector nears failure; failure is a latent fault hiding until a real emergency.
ideal_interaction: Clip the stress lead on each injector and turn its stress dial up one setting at a time, pulling back the instant the glow goes uneven or the whine rises.

label: Cold-start drill
human_steps: Read the cold-start checklist card on the console and confirm the crew stations.
Open the coolant feed valve first and confirm its flow lamp.
Energise the injector bank and check each injector's ignition light.
Bring the constrictors up one by one, watching each for a steady field.
Hold at the first output step through the stability count.
Sign the drill card with the time for each stage.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping the order strict and confirming each lamp before the next step; failure is a crew unprepared for restart.
ideal_interaction: Work the cold-start sequence on the console in checklist order, pressing each stage only after its prior lamp goes green, and stop the drill if a stage is pressed out of order.

label: Report all margins
human_steps: Sit at the engineering desk and open the margin report form.
Enter the core temperature margin from the core sheet.
Enter the coolant flow margin and the constrictor headroom from the trim sheet.
Enter the power margin from the budget and load sheets.
Check each figure against its source sheet, one line at a time.
Send the report to the bridge and wait for the receipt.
what_makes_it_hard: Pulling the current figure from several sheets and not mixing in an old one; failure is the bridge flying blind on its limits.
ideal_interaction: Fill the margin form line by line from the core, trim and budget sheets, checking each entry against its source sheet before sending to the bridge.

label: Patrol the ship
human_steps: Step out of the ready room and walk toward the cargo corridor, glancing at the tamper-seal lamps on each bulkhead panel
Walk the corridor with one hand trailing the bulkhead, trying each door latch with a firm pull
Stop at the mess and lounge doors and inspect frame seams and keypad housings for pry marks or loose screws
Look under lounge chairs and behind the replicator alcove for anything wedged or hidden
At each junction tap the wall log panel to record that the round passed
Return to the ready room and note any door that does not seat fully in the duty log
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a real tamper mark or a misaligned panel from ordinary wear, and noticing it at all, is the skill; failure is a walk that looks thorough but misses a pried seam.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the deck route with the handheld light and must hold it on each door seam for two seconds before the seam is marked clear; a pried seam only shows a glint at the right angle.

label: Inspect armory and chargers
human_steps: Sign the armory log on the wall slate with your own stylus
Open the locker and lift each zapper from its cradle, reading the power bar on its grip
Count the cradles against the log and note any empty one
Look at the charger rack lights: green means full, steady amber means cycling, flicker means fault
Press the test stud on each charger and listen for the relay click
Relock the locker and tug the seal to confirm it caught
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is telling a steady amber from a stuck amber; failure is signing the log while one cell is quietly half-charged.
ideal_interaction: Player lifts each zapper from its cradle, reads the power bar, then presses the charger test stud and waits for the relay click before the locker reseals; a stuck amber must be caught during the sweep.

label: Test internal sensors and force fields
human_steps: Walk to the brig console and wake the sensor panel, stepping around the cell door
Run the lifeform scan and watch the blip count for each deck section on the screen
Walk to the cell emitter housing and open its access plate with a hex key
Place a handheld field meter against the emitter grid and read the hum level
Cycle the emitters on and off from the console while watching the meter needle
Log each dead section on the fault slate and note which corridor it blinds
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a dead emitter from a weak one takes a steady reading across several cycles; failure is logging a field as good because the console said so while the meter sat flat.
ideal_interaction: Player moves a handheld field meter along the emitter grid while toggling the console; the needle must rise on each cycle, and a flat needle marks that section as blind.

label: Security status to XO
human_steps: Sit at the ready room desk and pull the incident list from the slate
Read each open item aloud and check its time stamp against the duty log
Mark the three most urgent items in red on the desk display
Call the XO on the comm and wait for the channel to open
Give a spoken brief, one item at a time, leaving room for questions
Write each order the XO gives on the margin of the slate and read it back
what_makes_it_hard: Choosing which items matter and reading back orders accurately under interruption; failure is a brief that buries the one urgent item or a misheard order.
ideal_interaction: Player works a live comm call: speaks short briefs into the handset while the XO interrupts at random, must pick the urgent item from a shuffled list in order, and must read back each order before it is accepted.
fit_note: A form lets the player fill fields, but the real work is briefing the XO aloud, choosing what matters and reading back orders.

label: Routine patrol and armory count
human_steps: Walk into the armory and check the door seal before stepping inside
Open the weapon locker and take inventory of each cradle by eye and by touch
Lift each zapper to feel its weight and read its grip cell
Compare the count to the previous line on the log slate
Ring any empty cradle with a pencil mark on the slate
Walk back out to the corridor and check the door panel light on your way
what_makes_it_hard: Counting every cradle once and only once while noticing a single missing cell; failure is a count that matches the log but not the rack.
ideal_interaction: Player counts the cradles by moving the cursor along the rack and selecting each zapper once; a double-tapped or skipped cradle changes the tally, which must be reconciled against the logged number.

label: Test brig force field and sensors
human_steps: Walk to the brig door and check the occupant through the viewport
Open the field panel and read the status lamp for each grid zone
Set a handheld field meter on the grid at three fixed points and read each value
Ask the prisoner through the grille whether they feel the field
Switch the field off and on from the panel lever and check the lamp changes each time
Note each reading and any flicker on the brig slate
what_makes_it_hard: Reading meter values at several points and noticing a flicker that a lamp hides; failure is a panel that looks green while one grid point is dead.
ideal_interaction: Player places the meter at three fixed points in turn, reading each needle, then pulls the panel lever and watches for a point whose needle stays low after the field recovers.
fit_note: A generic bench readout does not capture walking the grid with a handheld meter and checking the occupant.

label: Post a guard at the lab
human_steps: Walk to the lab door and check the status light and door seal
Look at the duty roster slate and find an officer rested enough for the post
Walk to that officer's station and brief them on what to watch for
Hand over the post log and have them sign in at the door panel
Walk back to the lab door and confirm the guard stands where you placed them
Note the post and time on the roster slate
what_makes_it_hard: Picking a fit officer and briefing them clearly enough that they hold the door; failure is a post left empty or given to someone exhausted.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the corridor to a crewman, selects them by touch, and walks them back to the lab door, where they must be placed on the marked spot and confirmed with a sign-in at the door panel.
fit_note: A roster menu assigns names; the real job is walking to the lab door, choosing a guard and placing them there in person.

label: Sweep sensors before the away team beams out
human_steps: Step onto the transporter pad and check the status board for an active beam window
Take the handheld sensor from its pad rail and set its range to close
Sweep the sensor slowly around the pad edge and across the platform rim
Read the sensor display for any lifesign or energy spike before the window closes
Call the transporter chief to say the pad is clear or to hold
Step off the pad and confirm the sensor log is saved to the bridge
what_makes_it_hard: Sweeping the whole pad area at a steady pace while catching a faint lifesign; failure is a clear call made while a contact still sits in the beam zone.
ideal_interaction: Player sweeps the handheld sensor in a slow arc around the pad, keeping the cursor on the sensor's edge; a blip must be held two seconds to register, and the player calls hold if one lingers in the beam zone.
fit_note: Patrol walks a corridor route; this job is a handheld sensor swept over a pad before a beam window.

label: Arm escort for away team
human_steps: Walk to the armory locker and sign the issue sheet with your name
Take each sidearm from its cradle and read its power bar
Pick one sidearm per away team member from the rack, reserving any with a low bar
Clip each holster to the person's belt and check the fit
Record each sidearm serial on the issue sheet against the person's name
Have each team member countersign the sheet before they leave
what_makes_it_hard: Matching sidearms to people and reading each power bar before issue; failure is an away team that beams down with a half-charged weapon.
ideal_interaction: Player lifts each sidearm from the rack, reads its power bar, then clips it to a named team member's holster; a low bar must be swapped out before the player can move on.
fit_note: A badge check verifies identity; arming an escort means issuing and checking charged sidearms.

label: Inspect cargo seals with the QM
human_steps: Walk to the cargo bay door and meet the quartermaster at the manifest board
Read the manifest sheet for crate numbers and seal colours
Walk along the crate stack and check each seal's serial against the manifest
Run a thumb along the seal bead to feel for a cut or a loose ring
Look for a band of off-colour seal that means it was swapped
Mark each mismatch on the manifest and sign the cargo tally
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting a swapped seal by colour and feel, and refusing to sign over a crate that does not match; failure is a tampered crate going aboard.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the crate stack with a cursor, comparing each seal's serial to the manifest; a swapped seal shows a shifted colour band that must be selected to flag before the tally can be signed.

label: Guard hold during loading
human_steps: Walk to the cargo corridor junction and stand where you can see both hatches
Watch each loader carry a crate past you and note its label
Count the crates going in against the loading tally on your wrist slate
Step forward when a loader pauses and ask them to show a pass
Look down the corridor for anyone lingering by an open locker
Radio the QM when the count is off by one
what_makes_it_hard: Holding attention on several moving crates and people at once while counting accurately; failure is a loader slipping an item out unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: Player stands at the junction and taps each crate on a passing conveyor of loaders; a crate that passes without a tap is counted as missing and must be chased down.
fit_note: Patrol walks a route; this job is standing still at a junction watching loaders and counting crates.

label: Escort and control the sickbay entrance
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay doors and look at the entrance corridor for crowding
Look at each person coming up and ask for their medical pass
Let staff through with a nod and hold the door for stretchers
Raise a palm to stop the crowd when the ward is full
Check the ward light: green to admit, red to hold
Radio the CMO when the queue backs up to the corridor corner
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping a steady flow through the door while turning people back; failure is a blocked stretcher or a crowd pushed through past the triage line.
ideal_interaction: Player stands at the sickbay door tapping each approaching figure, letting through those with a green pass and holding back the rest; the ward light must stay green and the queue must not block the stretcher lane.
fit_note: A badge check does not cover controlling crowd flow at a stretcher door.

label: Keep order among the evacuees
human_steps: Walk into the cargo corridor and find the knot of people by the bulkhead
Stand where the crowd can see you, hands visible and open
Speak to the loudest person by name and ask them to step aside
Move two people apart when one shoves the other
Walk the line and point the next group toward the bay
Give water from your carried flask to anyone who looks faint
what_makes_it_hard: Reading when calm talk will work and when to step between people; failure is a shove that turns into a brawl.
ideal_interaction: Player walks a corridor of agitated evacuees, using voice choices to pick who to address first; a shove must be defused by stepping between the two figures before the tension meter fills.
fit_note: A badge check does not reach crowd control; this job is talking people down and steering a crowd.

label: Check visitors for contamination risk
human_steps: Stand at the airlock inner door and check the visitor's arrival slip
Take a swab from the visitor's cheek with a sterile stick and seal it in a tube
Label the tube with the visitor's name and the time
Place the tube in the rack and set the sample chamber to scan
Read the scan lamp: amber means hold the visitor, green means pass
Hand the visitor a clean wrist band and state the ward rules
what_makes_it_hard: Taking a clean swab and reading an amber lamp correctly; failure is a contaminated visitor waved through on a green lamp that was not yet set.
ideal_interaction: Player swabs the visitor's cheek in a small arc, drops the tube into the rack and waits for the scan lamp; a premature green lamp is a mistake to catch before the visitor passes.

label: Test every security field and alarm
human_steps: Walk to the brig console and read the list of every field and alarm
Trip each alarm at its panel, one at a time, and listen for the sound
Walk to each field emitter and check its lamp changes on each trip
Log each alarm sound and lamp state on the test sheet
Put a test object into each beam to check the field holds it
Reset all alarms and confirm the console shows armed
what_makes_it_hard: Testing every alarm and field without skipping one; failure is a test sheet filled in for an alarm that never tripped.
ideal_interaction: Player trips each numbered alarm in turn and then checks its matching emitter lamp; a lamp that stays dark after its alarm trips must be flagged before the next item unlocks.

label: Run an intruder lockdown drill
human_steps: Walk to the bridge console and open the drill script
Choose the deck sections to seal and set a start time
Press the lockdown key and watch the door tell-tales turn red
Speak the drill order on the ship PA and listen for acknowledgements
Wait for each section lead to report sealed, then tick them off the list
Write the real seal time beside the planned time
what_makes_it_hard: Judging whether every section has truly sealed, not just reported it; failure is a drill that sounds fine while one tell-tale stayed green.
ideal_interaction: Player arms the lockdown key, then watches door tell-tales light up on the deck plan and presses each section's confirm only once its door has turned red; a door still green after the timer is a failed seal.
fit_note: A PA announcement misses the physical sealing and checking of doors.

label: Armory charger load test
human_steps: Open the armory locker and take the test cells from their cradle
Seat each cell in a charger slot and press it home until it clicks
Read the charge meter on each slot as the load climbs
Note the time each cell takes to reach full on the test sheet
Pull any cell that heats past the warning line and set it aside
Tag each slow charger for engineering on the test sheet
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a slow charger from a dying cell by timing each against the others; failure is a charger logged as fine when it never reached full.
ideal_interaction: Player seats each power cell into a slot with a click, then watches each slot's meter climb against a timer; a slot that climbs slowly or hits the heat line must be tagged before the cell can be cleared.

label: Deck patrol and door checks
human_steps: Meet the security officer at the cargo corridor and take the route card
Walk the route and touch each door panel to test the lock seats
Check each door seal for a gap or a bent strip
Look up at the camera housing and check the picture by waving at it
Hold a badge to each reader and confirm it beeps
Write any anomaly on the route card at the door where it was seen
what_makes_it_hard: Testing every lock and reader without skipping one; failure is a door logged as secure when its lock never seated.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the route alongside an officer and presses a badge to each reader; a reader that fails to beep marks its door, and the player must pull the handle to test the seal before moving on.

label: Armory inventory audit
human_steps: Check each locker seal for a broken tamper strip
Open the locker and count the weapons on each rack
Count the charge packs and read each one's gauge
Compare the count to the sign-out log held in your other hand
Countersign the audit sheet with your own stylus
Recount any mismatch with the armory officer before you sign
what_makes_it_hard: Counting without double-counting, and recounting a mismatch before accusing anyone; failure is a count sent up that a gap in the rack already hid.
ideal_interaction: Player counts weapons and packs by moving a cursor across each rack, marking each once; a shortfall against the sign-out total shows as a red tally that must be recounted before the countersign unlocks.

label: Brig and cell field-check
human_steps: Walk to the brig console and check the welfare board for each cell
Walk to each cell door and check the field lamp on its frame
Read the cell log and check the last entry for each occupant
Look through each viewport and check the occupant is breathing and moving
Note any cell whose lamp is dim or whose occupant is unresponsive
Log the field check and sign the welfare board
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a dim field lamp from a normal one and noticing an occupant who has stopped moving; failure is a silent cell left unchecked overnight.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the cell row, pausing at each viewport to watch the occupant's breathing; a still figure or a dim lamp opens a welfare alert that must be cleared before the board can be signed.

label: Roster and readiness review
human_steps: Sit at the brig desk and open the duty roster on the slate
Read each officer's rest record and last shift end time
Mark anyone short on rest in amber
Drag two names on the shift grid to swap their shifts into the open slots
Check each swapped officer's new shift against their rest record
Flag any weak coverage to the Chief in the handover note
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting who is genuinely exhausted and balancing swaps without leaving a post empty; failure is a swap that leaves a gap for the night watch.
ideal_interaction: Player drags officer names around a shift grid, and each move updates a rest bar; a swap that drops a post below minimum or leaves someone on too little rest turns red and must be undone.

label: Run routine patrol and door checks
human_steps: Step out of the cargo bay into the corridor and face the route marker
Walk to each door in turn and test its handle with a firm pull
Stop at each junction and look up at the camera lens for smudges
Tap the door's badge reader with a card to confirm the beep
Glance into any side alcove and note loose items or open lockers
Log each door as secure on the wall panel as you pass it
what_makes_it_hard: Completing a full check alone without a second pair of eyes; failure is a door that looks latched but gives under a firm pull.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the corridor solo, pulling each door handle in turn; a door that gives under the pull must be flagged before the wall log lets the player mark that section secure.

label: Armory audit
human_steps: Walk to the armory and check the door log for last night's entries
Stand at the locker and count the weapons by hand
Count the charge packs and read their gauges
Compare your count against the door log's sign-out times
Note any item missing and any sign-out with no matching return
Sign the audit and tell the Chief if the numbers differ
what_makes_it_hard: Matching a physical count to door-log entries that do not line up neatly; failure is a missing weapon explained away as a clerical error.
ideal_interaction: Player counts the rack by hand, then ticks entries on a door-log timeline; any unmatched sign-out leaves a gap the player must chase by selecting the missing item in the rack.
fit_note: Reading a door log scrolls text; the real audit counts the physical weapons and packs in the locker.

label: Restrict lab and sensor access to survey personnel
human_steps: Stand at the lab door and check the access list on the door panel
Hold out a hand to each person approaching and ask for their badge
Read the badge's name and clearance against the list
Turn back anyone without clearance and point them to the bridge
Watch the door behind admitted people for anyone tailgating through
Log each admit with the time on the access slate
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting a tailgater and turning away someone with a plausible story; failure is an unauthorised person slipping in behind a cleared one.
ideal_interaction: Player stands at the lab door tapping each approaching badge against the access list; a second figure slipping in behind a cleared one must be caught with a tap before the door closes.
fit_note: Badge reading alone misses logging admits and watching for tailgaters at the door.

label: Post an officer at the shuttlebay for away-team traffic
human_steps: Walk to the shuttlebay door and check the bay status board
Pick a rested officer from the roster who is fit for the post
Walk that officer to the shuttlebay door and brief them on the traffic log
Set them on the post spot and confirm they have the log stylus
Check back an hour later that they are still at the post
Mark the post as filled on the roster slate
what_makes_it_hard: Choosing an officer who can hold a post through quiet hours and briefing them to log every crossing; failure is a post left unmanned during an away-team return.
ideal_interaction: Player walks an officer from the roster to the shuttlebay door and places them on the marked post, where they must log each crossing the player triggers in order; leaving the post before the flight ends fails it.
fit_note: A roster menu assigns names; the real post is physically placing an officer at the door.

label: Routine patrol with reduced staff
human_steps: Take the reduced route card and note which decks are uncovered
Walk the cargo corridor and cover the doors nearest the bay first
Walk to the junction where the second officer would normally stand
Look down each branch and sweep the corner lights with your eyes
Radio the bridge the sector you are covering
Return the route card with the uncovered sections marked
what_makes_it_hard: Judging which uncovered sections are riskiest when you cannot cover them all; failure is a gap at a junction the thinned patrol never reaches.
ideal_interaction: Player walks a shortened route with a radio, choosing which uncovered branch to sweep at each junction; a branch left unchecked too long lights a warning that must be answered by returning to it.

label: Inspect manifest and seals with the deck chief
human_steps: Meet the deck chief at the cargo door and take the manifest board
Read the crate count and seal colours on the manifest
Walk the stack and compare each seal's number to the sheet
Press a thumb on each seal to feel for a cut or a loose ring
Mark any mismatched crate with a red chalk line on the door
Countersign the manifest once every crate matches
what_makes_it_hard: Matching many seal numbers accurately and feeling for a tampered ring; failure is a countersigned manifest that hides a swapped crate.
ideal_interaction: Player holds the seal scanner to each crate in turn, letting the beep confirm a match; a silent scanner marks the crate for the chief, and the countersign stays locked until every crate beeps.

label: Guard transporter pad during transfers
human_steps: Stand at the transporter pad with a clear view of the operator console
Check each transfer order and its signature against the list
Watch the pad for anything that is not on the order
Look at the operator's readout before each beam
Stop an unsigned transfer by stepping onto the pad edge
Log each completed transfer and its time
what_makes_it_hard: Holding attention through many transfers and stopping an unsigned one without holding up the bridge; failure is an unsigned crate beamed out unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: Player stands on the pad edge and taps each transfer order as it appears; an unsigned order flashes red and the player must step onto the pad to hold the beam before it fires.
fit_note: A badge check does not cover verifying signed orders and holding a transfer before it fires.

label: Lock cargo bay after loading
human_steps: Walk to the cargo bay door once the last crate is in
Count the crates in the bay against the loaded manifest
Pull the hatch down and listen for the seal to catch
Turn the bay lock key and check its status lamp reads locked
Walk the bay perimeter and try each hatch by hand
Log the lock time and sign the bay log
what_makes_it_hard: Confirming the lock actually caught on every hatch, not just the main door; failure is a hatch left open while its lamp read sealed.
ideal_interaction: Player pulls each hatch down with a firm hold and listens for the click; a hatch that does not click leaves its lamp amber, and the player must go back and re-seat it before the lock key can turn.

label: Escort patients and clear a corridor to sickbay
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay door and look down the corridor for blockers
Ask the crowd to step back and point to the stretcher lane
Walk ahead of the stretcher and stop anyone standing in its path
Hold a door open at each junction with a foot or a hand
Check the stretcher's rear is clear of the corner rail
Log the clear time with the CMO and stay at the door
what_makes_it_hard: Clearing a path without shoving people and holding a door without letting it close on the stretcher; failure is a jam at a corner.
ideal_interaction: Player walks ahead of the stretcher tapping each person in the path to step aside; a person left standing in the lane blocks the stretcher bar until a second tap clears them.

label: Control access to quarantine area
human_steps: Stand at the quarantine door and check the ward pass board
Ask each visitor for a screening slip and read its date
Hand masks to anyone without one and watch them put it on
Sign visitors in on the quarantine log with the time
Turn away anyone whose screening slip is out of date
Check the log at shift end for anyone not signed out
what_makes_it_hard: Turning away a sympathetic visitor with an out-of-date slip; failure is someone entering the ward on an expired screen.
ideal_interaction: Player faces each visitor at the quarantine door and reads the date on their slip; an expired date must be refused, and a mask handed over before the door will open.
fit_note: A badge check misses reading screening slips and handing out masks.

label: Keep the peace in mess and lounge
human_steps: Walk to the mess table and sit where both sides can see you
Listen to each person's complaint in turn without interrupting
Repeat back the main point of each grievance in your own words
Ask both sides what they would accept and write it on the table pad
Split up two people who are leaning in too close
Check back with each group before leaving the table
what_makes_it_hard: Listening long enough to find the real grievance and getting both sides to agree; failure is a quarrel that resumes the moment the officer walks away.
ideal_interaction: Player sits at the table and selects each speaker in turn to hear their complaint, then picks which points to repeat; a point repeated wrongly makes that person pull back, and it must be restated to win them round.

label: Drill intruder lockdown with security staff
human_steps: Walk to the brig console and gather the security staff around the table
Call out the drill scenario and assign each officer a deck
Start the timer and send each officer to lock their assigned door
Walk the corridor behind them checking each door is sealed
Ask each officer to report by name when their door is locked
Note any officer who lagged and debrief them on the spot
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping the drill realistic, spotting a door that looks sealed but is not, and debriefing without blame; failure is a drill that passes on paper with a door still open.
ideal_interaction: Player assigns officers to doors on a deck plan and starts the timer; each officer must be dispatched to a door, and the player traces each seal along the corridor, sending back any door whose seal shows a gap.
fit_note: Locking a single cargo hatch does not capture running a multi-officer drill and checking every seal.

label: Test armory release and badge locks
human_steps: Walk to the armory door and read the badge lock's status lamp
Hold your own badge to the reader and watch the lock release
Try a second, unauthorised badge and check the lock refuses it
Test the locker release lever by hand and feel the latch
Check the emergency release works without a badge
Log the release result for each locker on the test sheet
what_makes_it_hard: Testing the emergency release without a badge and confirming a refused badge truly locks out; failure is a locker that opens for the wrong badge.
ideal_interaction: Player swipes each test badge across the reader in turn; authorised badges release the lock, the emergency lever must be pulled by hand, and any lock that opens for the wrong badge is marked failed.
fit_note: A badge check alone does not test the emergency release or the refusal by hand.

label: Report drill results to the bridge
human_steps: Sit at the bridge console and pull up the drill log
Enter each officer's seal time into the form, one row at a time
Mark any door that did not seal in red on the form
Write a short account of what went wrong in the comments box
Check that the totals match the number of doors on the deck plan
Submit the form and wait for the bridge acknowledgement
what_makes_it_hard: Entering each time and door accurately without skipping a red-flag door; failure is a clean form submitted while a seal failure sits in the log.
ideal_interaction: Player types each door's seal time into the form and checks it against the drill log, and red-flag rows must be completed before the submit key will work.

label: Patrol round of crew decks
human_steps: Walk out of the quarters corridor and take the route on your wrist slate
Try each door latch in turn with a firm pull
Scan the corridor corners for strangers or anything out of place
Look at each wall panel for scratches or pry marks
Stop at the wall log panel and tap your round
Note anything odd on the panel before moving on
what_makes_it_hard: Trying every latch and noticing small damage; failure is a round logged with a stuck latch left unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the crew corridor pulling each door handle; a latch that gives reveals a fault to log, and the round only completes once every wall panel has been tapped.

label: Hold post at brig or transporter
human_steps: Walk to the brig post and stand where you can see the door and panel
Check the force-field panel lamp and read its status
Look at each person who approaches the brig door
Ask unknown people for a badge and read it
Note each visitor on the post log with name and time
Call the Security Officer if anyone refuses
what_makes_it_hard: Staying alert through long quiet stretches and challenging a stranger without being rude; failure is a visitor let through unchallenged.
ideal_interaction: Player stands at the brig post watching figures approach and taps each to challenge them; the player reads each badge and turns away an unbadged figure before it reaches the door.
fit_note: Badge checks are only part of the post; the job also includes reading the field panel and logging visitors.

label: Armory sign-out and charge check
human_steps: Walk to the armory locker and sign your name on the sign-out sheet
Count the sidearms on the rack by hand
Lift a sidearm from its cradle and read the grip charge indicator
Check each charger light is green, not amber
Reconcile your count against the sheet entries
Report any shortfall or low charge to the Security Officer
what_makes_it_hard: Counting and reading each grip indicator reliably; failure is a sidearm handed out with low charge because the count was rushed.
ideal_interaction: Player lifts each sidearm from its cradle to read the grip indicator and returns it to the right slot; a low charge must be swapped before the sign-out sheet can be countersigned.
fit_note: A badge check verifies identity; this job counts and reads sidearm charge and reconciles a sheet.

label: Routine patrol of all decks
human_steps: Begin at the lowest deck corridor and climb the ladder to the next landing
At each deck landing, press the lift door seal and check it holds
Walk the length of each corridor at a steady pace
Pause at each junction and listen for voices behind closed doors
Note any light or alarm lamp that is out
Finish at the quarters corridor and log the full round
what_makes_it_hard: Covering every deck evenly and listening through closed doors; failure is a deck skipped because the shift was quiet.
ideal_interaction: Player walks a set of decks up a ladder, stopping at each landing to press the lift seal and listen; a skipped landing blocks the round log until the player goes back to it.

label: Hold post at brig door
human_steps: Walk to the brig door and take up the post stance
Look through the grille at the prisoner and note how they are sitting
Check the field panel lamp at the door frame every few minutes
Refuse entry to anyone without a badge and call it in
Note the time of each check on the post slate
Hand over the post by reading the slate aloud to the relief
what_makes_it_hard: Staying alert through a long quiet post and seeing a prisoner change before it becomes trouble; failure is a fallen prisoner noticed too late.
ideal_interaction: Player holds the brig post and glances through the grille at the prisoner on a timer; a prisoner who stops moving must be reported before the post timer lets the player move on.
fit_note: Holding a door post is more than badge checking; the job also involves monitoring the prisoner and field lamp.

label: Guard the science lab entrance during sensor sweeps
human_steps: Walk to the lab entrance and check the status board for sweep times
Stand beside the door where the sensor operators can see you
Check each person entering against the sweep list
Ask anyone carrying sample cases to show the case seal
Turn back anyone not on the list and call the science officer
Keep the door clear while the sweep runs and log the times
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping sensitive data out during a live sweep without letting a scientist's urgency push you aside; failure is an unauthorised person reaching the sample room.
ideal_interaction: Player stands at the lab entrance tapping each arrival against the sweep list; anyone carrying a sample case must show the seal, and anyone off the list is turned away.
fit_note: A badge check misses checking sample case seals and maintaining the sweep list.

label: Check internal sensors cover the main corridors
human_steps: Walk to the start of the main corridor with the handheld coverage meter
Hold the meter at chest height and walk slowly along the wall
Watch the meter for a dip where the reading falls to zero
Mark each blind spot on the wall panel with a grease pencil
Walk back and check each blind spot again from the other direction
Report the blind spots to the Security Officer in the log
what_makes_it_hard: Walking slowly enough to see a dip and checking from both directions; failure is a blind spot missed because it was only found on one pass.
ideal_interaction: Player walks a corridor holding a coverage meter at chest height; a dip in the needle must be marked by pressing the wall, then the player re-walks it from the other side to confirm.
fit_note: Fieldsweep is a console test; the job is a handheld walk with a coverage meter to find blind spots.

label: Watch cargo seals during loading
human_steps: Walk to the cargo bay door and read the seal numbers on the board
Watch each crate as it is lifted past the door
Compare each seal's number to the loading list
Feel the seal bead for cuts or a loose ring
Mark any crate with a missing or doubled seal with chalk
Call the Security Officer before the next crate is lifted
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping track of seals on a fast loading line; failure is a crate carrying a doubled seal that goes aboard.
ideal_interaction: Player watches crates move along the loading line and taps each seal number to match it against the list; a doubled seal flashes and needs a chalk mark before the crate can pass.

label: Badge check at shuttlebay
human_steps: Stand at the shuttlebay door with the badge reader at your right hand
Ask each person boarding to hold their badge to the reader
Read the name on the reader display and check it against the manifest
Ask anyone without a badge to step aside
Note each person boarded with time and name
Wave the next person forward when the reader beeps clear
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping the line moving while catching a person with no badge; failure is an unlogged crate or person leaving the ship.
ideal_interaction: Player taps each boarding figure's badge against the reader; a badge with the wrong name flashes red, and a figure with no badge must be waved aside before the line moves on.

label: Escort valuables to the transporter
human_steps: Walk to the valuables store and sign the transfer chit
Take the valuables case from the clerk and check its seal number
Walk the case through the corridor to the transporter, keeping it at your side
Stop at each corner and check the case handle is tight
Hand the case to the transporter operator and get a receipt
Stay at the pad until the beam completes and log the receipt
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping a hand on the case all the way without being distracted; failure is an unsupervised handoff at the pad.
ideal_interaction: Player carries the case along the corridor with a hold-and-release grip on the handle; the case slides if the grip loosens at a corner, and a dropped case must be retrieved before the handoff can be signed.

label: Control the corridor to sickbay and keep it clear
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay door and check the corridor path is open
Stand at the corridor corner where people turn toward sickbay
Ask anyone blocking the path to step back to the wall
Keep the stretcher lane clear with an outstretched arm
Check the ward door is latched after each stretcher passes
Log the clear time and call the Security Officer if it jams
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping the path clear without manhandling anyone; failure is a stretcher stuck at a corner while the corridor stays crowded.
ideal_interaction: Player holds a corner pad on the corridor wall and drags each blocker to the wall; the stretcher lane light only turns green once every figure is clear of the path.

label: Escort medical supplies from stores
human_steps: Walk to the stores door and sign the supply chit
Take the supply crate from the shelf and check its label matches the chit
Carry the crate with both arms, looking over it at each step
Walk the route to sickbay without setting it down in corridors
Hand the crate to the medical orderly and get their signature
Log the handover time on the chit
what_makes_it_hard: Carrying the crate steadily past crowds and checking the label before handover; failure is the wrong supplies arriving in sickbay.
ideal_interaction: Player stacks boxes on a trolley and steers it through corridor turns; a box that tips off must be re-stacked before the orderly will sign, and the label is read against the chit first.

label: Armory readiness check and drill
human_steps: Walk into the armory and check the readiness board for the drill order
Count the weapons on each rack and compare to the sign-out sheet
Check each charger light and note any amber
Lift one sidearm from the rack and test its trigger click
Call out the drill scenario and watch the officers arm up
Log the drill time and any gap in the readiness count
what_makes_it_hard: Counting and testing under time pressure and calling out gaps; failure is a drill that starts with the armory one weapon short.
ideal_interaction: Player arms the drill by taking sidearms from the rack one by one under a timer, reading each trigger click; a missing or dead sidearm must be reported before the drill clock stops.

label: Test brig force-field panel
human_steps: Walk to the brig force-field panel and open its cover
Read the status lamp for each field zone
Press the test stud and watch each zone flicker and recover
Listen for a zone that is silent or hums out of pattern
Log each zone's response on the panel tag
Close the cover and tug the lock to confirm it seated
what_makes_it_hard: Hearing a wrong hum in a zone and telling a real dead zone from a flicker; failure is a silent emitter reported as normal.
ideal_interaction: Player presses the test stud on each zone in turn and watches its lamp flicker; a zone whose lamp stays dark or hums wrong must be marked on the tag before the cover can close.
fit_note: A bench tests a generic readout; the job is opening the panel and checking each zone's lamp and sound.

label: Station for intruder drill
human_steps: Walk to the transporter door and report to the drill controller
Stand at the door with your back to the pad, facing the corridor
Check each person coming through against the drill roster
Hold the door closed when the lockdown tone sounds
Confirm the lockdown light is red on the door panel
Report to the controller once the door is sealed
what_makes_it_hard: Holding a door under drill pressure and staying calm while people push against it; failure is a door that gives under the crowd.
ideal_interaction: Player stands at the transporter door as drill figures press toward it and must keep a hold button down to brace it; if the grip slips someone gets through, and the lockdown light must be red before the drill passes.
fit_note: Badge checks are only one part; the drill station is holding and sealing the door against pressure.

label: Grow bed round
human_steps: Walk the bed rows in order, starting at the sealed tray nearest the door
Lift the cover on each tray and look at leaf colour: yellowing at the tips means nitrogen is low
Push a probe into the root zone, read the moisture meter, then wipe the probe on a cloth
Read the pH strip dipped in the drain runoff and compare it against the green band on the card
Turn the dial on any pump that reads outside band, then wait for the flow gauge to settle
Pinch-check undersides of leaves for aphids and note any grey film in the log slate
what_makes_it_hard: The judgement is reading a slow plant signal early and adjusting one pump without overdosing; failure is a flooded bed or a crop lost to a pest missed under the leaves.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the bed rows, probes each tray with the moisture probe, reads the pH strip against the band, and turns pump dials until the gauges sit in the green, with overdosing flooding the tray.

label: O2 reclamation check
human_steps: Sit at the lab console and open the scrubber telemetry for the last twelve hours
Pull the O2 output trace from the arboretum and set it beside the crew load board
Compare the two curves, looking for a gap that grows over the shift rather than a single spike
Check the reclaimer filter pressure gauge reading against its last service mark
Write a one-line drift note with the percentage gap and the time it began
Send the note to environmental with the reclaimer status ticked or flagged
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is telling a real slow decline from normal night-cycle dips and naming the cause before it reaches a crisis; failure is a false alarm or a missed creeping gap.
ideal_interaction: The player overlays two live curves on the trace viewer, scrubs the timeline to find where the gap starts widening, and drags a marker to the onset point before filing the drift note.

label: Harvest for galley
human_steps: Walk to the fruiting rack and check the colour chart on each pod for ripeness
Twist ripe produce from the stalk with a thumb pressure, leaving the stem on
Drop each pick into a shallow basket and reject any split or mould-marked fruit into the bin
Rinse the basket under the sluice tap and dry each piece on a clean towel
Pack the crate in layers with leaf padding and stamp the crate with the picking time
Carry the crate to the galley hatch and hand it to the cook with a tally slip
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is judging ripeness by colour and firmness without bruising, and not picking early; failure is wasted crop from premature picks or bruised produce that spoils in the galley.
ideal_interaction: The player moves along the fruiting rack, compares each pod against the colour chart, presses lightly to test firmness, and twists only the ripe ones into the basket, where an over-hard twist drops the pod in the bin.

label: Routine bed round and logs
human_steps: Walk the bed rows with the log slate and tick each tray as checked
Look at each tray surface for fungal bloom or wilting along the stem edge
Read the water level tube on each tray and top it from the reservoir jug if low
Write any change in the log slate, such as a new brown leaf edge, with the tray number
Wipe the slate and return it to the hook by the door
Note in the log whether all trays passed, so the next shift starts clean
what_makes_it_hard: The job is a quiet watch where the skill is noticing a small change on a routine round and logging it exactly; failure is skipping a tray or logging a vague note that the next shift cannot act on.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the tray rows, checks the water tube on each tray and tops it from the jug when low, and logs each tray; skipping a tray leaves a gap in the log that the game flags.
fit_note: Same growbed activity as the main round, but this task is a logging round with less physical probing.

label: Harvest for galley
human_steps: Check the galley order slip for what the cook asked for today
Walk the rack looking at the top pods first, since those are ripest on the day
Cut each chosen stem with the snips about a finger's width above the node
Place stems in a wet tray so they do not wilt before the galley
Count the pick against the order slip and mark any shortfall in pencil
Carry the wet tray to the galley and leave the count with the cook
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is matching a quantity order to what the rack can give without cutting too much and leaving the plant weak; failure is a short order or an over-cut plant that stops fruiting.
ideal_interaction: The player reads the order slip, snips stems at the node with a steady cut, and watches a count bar fill; cutting too far above the node drops the stem and costs the plant a fruit.

label: Collect and log any alien spores or biological samples
human_steps: Walk to the sample bench and put on a gloved pair with the lab seal on
Open the sealed field pack and lift each vial with forceps to the light
Swab any residue on the outer case into a clean tube and cap it immediately
Seal each tube in a bag, write the site code and time with a grease pencil
Set the tube in the rack and scan its label into the sample log
Wipe the bench and bin the glove if the seal tears, then log the breach
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is containment: taking a sample without breaking the seal or contaminating the next tube; failure is cross-contamination or a broken seal that ruins the sample.
ideal_interaction: The player lifts vials with forceps, swabs residue into a tube and caps it fast, and a seal-check meter drops if the glove touches the outer case.

label: Quarantine-check samples against the beds
human_steps: Pull the sample tube from the rack and read its site code on the label
Open the bed roster on the lab console and find the bed that matches the code
Look at the sample under the hand lens and note leaf or spore shape
Compare the sample shape to the bed species card and mark match, near or no match
Clip a red tag onto any tube with a no-match result and move it to the quarantine shelf
Log each tube result and the bed it was checked against
what_makes_it_hard: The judgement is comparing a physical sample against the species card and calling a match, near or no match; failure is a false clear that lets a foreign spore into the beds.
ideal_interaction: The player takes a sample tube, matches its code to a bed on the roster, then compares it against the species card under the lens and chooses match, near or no match, with a wrong clear letting spores into the beds.
fit_note: Uses the sample collection activity, but the real work is comparing the sample against the bed records and the species card.

label: Boost O2 output for sensor crew on extended shifts
human_steps: Check the extended shift roster and the sensor crew's head count in the hold
Walk to the lamp array and read each lamp's output dial against its rated level
Raise the lamp intensity in small steps and watch the light meter at the tray
Dial the nutrient feed up a notch on the beds nearest the sensor crew's quarters
Wait a full cycle then read the O2 output gauge to confirm the rise
Log the new settings and the gauge reading before the next shift
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is pushing output up in small steps so the plants do not burn or starve; failure is lamp scorch or a nutrient burn that drops the output the crew needs.
ideal_interaction: The player raises the lamp dial in small steps while watching the light meter, then sets the nutrient feed; a sudden jump scorches the tray and lowers the O2 gauge.
fit_note: A nutrient dosing game only; the real work also involves the lamp intensity and light balance.

label: Inspect incoming plant stock and soil cargo
human_steps: Walk to the incoming crate stack and read the manifest tag on each crate
Pry open the top crate and lift the plant trays to look for leaf spots or webbing
Push a probe into the soil sacks and smell the sample for rot or sulphur
Check the root balls for grey mould and dark slime at the base
Mark any crate with spots or rot with a red stripe and move it to the quarantine bay
Sign the inspection sheet with the crate number and pass or fail
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is spotting early blight or rot by sight, smell and feel before it spreads to the beds; failure is a passed crate that brings blight into the arboretum.
ideal_interaction: The player pries crates open, runs a soil probe through each sack and lifts the trays to inspect the leaves with a magnifier, stripe-marking any crate with spots or rot; passing a rotten crate lets blight spread.

label: Move quarantined seedlings to the arboretum
human_steps: Pick up the quarantine seed tray from the shelf and check its seal tag
Carry the tray level down the corridor, avoiding bumps to the root plugs
At the arboretum door, look for the acclimation bay and the open slot
Set the tray on the slot and slide each seedling plug into its cell
Check that each root plug sits firm and that no leaf is folded under
Tick the transfer in the log and remove the quarantine tag
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is moving fragile seedlings without shaking the root plugs or folding leaves; failure is lost seedlings from rough handling or a plug left loose in its cell.
ideal_interaction: The player carries the seed tray along the corridor keeping it level, then slides each plug into its slot; tilting the tray too far lets the plugs fall out.

label: Prepare medicinal herbs and extracts for sickbay
human_steps: Read the sickbay dose sheet for the herb and the amount needed
Weigh the dried leaf on the balance to the exact gram on the sheet
Grind the leaf in the mortar with a steady circular motion until fine
Add the measured solvent to the flask and swirl it gently in the bath
Filter the liquid through the cloth into the amber vial and cap it tight
Label the vial with herb, dose, strength and time and set it in the chill box
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is dosing to the gram and keeping the extract clean and labelled; failure is a wrong dose or an unlabelled vial that could harm a patient.
ideal_interaction: The player reads the dose sheet, weighs the leaf to the target gram on the balance, grinds it in the mortar and measures solvent into the flask, where an overdose on the balance flags the vial as unsafe.

label: Deliver extracts to sickbay
human_steps: Pick up the labelled vials from the chill box and check each label against the order
Carry the vials in the padded case down the corridor and into sickbay
Walk to the biobed and find the nurse, then read the patient name on the chart
Hand the vial over and say the dose out loud so the nurse can confirm
Wait for the nurse to sign the delivery slip with the time
Stow the empty case and log the drop
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is matching the right dose to the right patient and getting a verbal confirmation; failure is a wrong patient or a missing signature that leaves the dose unverified.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the vials to the biobed, matches the patient chart to the label, and speaks the dose before the nurse signs; a mismatch sends the vial back.

label: Raise O2 output for the extra patients
human_steps: Check the extra patient count on the sickbay board before starting
Walk to the beds nearest the sickbay corridor and read each tray's output
Raise the lamp dial and nutrient feed on the front three trays only
Hold the light meter over the leaves and wait for the reading to climb
Read the O2 gauge to confirm the rise matches the patient need
Log the changes and the new gauge reading for the sickbay watch
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is raising output where the patients need it without scorching or starving the trays; failure is a burnt tray or a gauge that never rises.
ideal_interaction: The player raises the front trays' lamp dial and nutrient feed in small steps while watching the light meter climb, with a jump too fast burning the tray.
fit_note: Growbed round activity; it does not show the targeted, patient-linked O2 raise that the job asks for.

label: Full O2 output test of the beds
human_steps: Set the test cycle timer and note the start time in the test log
Walk the trays and place a sensor on each tray's leaf canopy
Read the O2 output at each sensor every fifteen minutes through the cycle
Mark any tray whose output dips below its rated line in red on the sheet
Shut the lamps off at the end of the cycle and wait for the reading to settle
Write the full output table and the tray with the lowest result on the test log
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is running a full cycle and reading each tray at the right time without skipping a reading; failure is a gap in the data or a tray missed in the table.
ideal_interaction: The player sets the test timer, places canopy sensors on each tray, and reads output at each interval on the trend; an unrecorded reading leaves a gap in the table.

label: Verify nutrient pump power draw
human_steps: Pick up the clamp meter and set the scale to amps on the bench
Clip the meter jaw around one pump lead, keeping hands off the bare wire
Start the pump on the bench panel and read the draw on the meter as it settles
Compare the draw against the spec plate on the pump housing
Repeat for each pump and mark any pump over the rated draw
Log the draws and the spec numbers in the maintenance slate
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is reading a clamp meter at steady state and comparing it to the spec without touching live wire; failure is a misread draw or a shock from a bare lead.
ideal_interaction: The player clamps the meter around each pump lead, starts the pump, and reads the draw as it settles; clamping while the pump is running reads the surge, not the steady draw.

label: Reconcile sensor data with master chart
human_steps: Pull the latest sensor sweep file from the intake slot on the lab console
Open the master chart beside it and align the two on the same grid origin
Walk the star list row by row, comparing each sensor position to its chart position
Measure the offset with the ruler tool and mark any body off by more than the tolerance
Tag unknown bodies with a new id and note the sweep time beside each one
Commit the revision only after every flagged row has a note
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is measuring real offsets and telling true drift from sensor noise before committing a revision; failure is a committed false drift or a missed shift in the master chart.
ideal_interaction: The player aligns the sweep over the master chart, measures each star offset with the ruler, and only commits once every off-tolerance body is flagged; committing early leaves an error in the chart.
fit_note: A generic verify check; it does not show the offset measuring against the grid that the real reconcile needs.

label: Hand updated plot to navigation
human_steps: Walk from the lab to the bridge with the plot case under one arm
Wait at the nav station until the navigator clears you to approach
Load the plot onto the nav console and watch the screen confirm the load
Point at each hazard mark on the screen and ask the navigator to confirm it aloud
Wait for the navigator to nod or name a different hazard
Log the handoff and the names of who confirmed the hazards
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is a clean verbal handoff where each hazard is confirmed by a person, not just loaded; failure is a hazard left unconfirmed that the navigator steers into.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the plot to the bridge, loads it onto the nav console, then taps each hazard and waits for the navigator's confirmation line; skipping a hazard tap leaves it unconfirmed.
fit_note: A form fill; the real handoff is a physical walk and a spoken confirmation of each hazard.

label: Back up chart database
human_steps: Walk to the datacore console and wait for the access light to turn green
Open the chart database and run the checksum tool on the full file
Compare the checksum against the value on the last backup record
Write the backup to the cold store slot and wait for the write light
Read the new backup's checksum and confirm it matches the source
Log the result with the time, checksum and backup slot number
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is verifying the copy against the source with a checksum before trusting the backup; failure is a corrupt backup that looks fine until someone restores it.
ideal_interaction: The player runs the checksum on the source, writes the backup, and checks the copy's checksum against the source; a mismatch marks the backup as failed.

label: Routine chart audit and drift check
human_steps: Open the chart audit list and pull the sector that is due for a check
Scan the star positions on the trend plot for any slow change from last week
Compare the current drift value with the value logged at the last audit
Note any star whose drift grows over three audits in a row
Flag the sector as clean or drifting on the audit list
Save the audit with the time and the sector name
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is seeing a slow drift across many audits rather than one large jump; failure is a star that creeps off the chart while every single audit looks acceptable.
ideal_interaction: The player steps through the trend plot one audit at a time and watches each star's drift line; a star creeping upward across three audits turns the sector flag amber.

label: Send updated plot to navigation
human_steps: Check the sent queue on the nav console for the plot's current version
Walk to the nav station with the plot version number written on your slate
