Send the plot file to the nav console and wait for the receipt line
Read the receipt and check the version number matches your slate
Ask the navigator for a quick word that the plot is in use
Log the send with the version and the receipt time
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is confirming the right version reached the nav console, not just that a send happened; failure is navigation using an old plot after a silent send.
ideal_interaction: The player sends the plot, then checks the receipt version against the slate; an old version in the receipt triggers a resend.
fit_note: A send form; the real check is matching the version receipt and the navigator confirming use.

label: Stage survey grid and target list
human_steps: Open the survey brief and read the sector bounds and target count
Lay out the grid cells on the console in rows that match the bounds
Drag each target from the candidate pool into a cell and set its priority
Check that no target sits on the grid edge or overlaps another cell
Sort the target list by priority and freeze it for the sweep
Save the staged grid and the list with the brief's reference number
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is laying out a grid that covers the sector without gaps or overlaps while ranking targets by priority; failure is a gap in coverage the sweep will never see.
ideal_interaction: The player drags targets into the grid cells and sets priorities, where a target dropped on a grid edge or a gap in coverage is flagged before freezing.

label: Ingest sensor sweep and render the survey chart
human_steps: Load the sweep file from the intake slot and confirm the sweep time stamp
Check the sweep's gain and noise readings against the calibration sheet
Import the points onto the survey grid and watch them plot in their cells
Classify each cluster as star, planet, debris or unknown using its signature band
Render the finished chart and check the scale bar matches the grid
Save the chart with its sweep time and the count of unknown bodies
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is classifying clusters by their signature band rather than guessing from position; failure is a debris cluster marked as a planet and sent on a false course.
ideal_interaction: The player imports the sweep, then taps each cluster and picks a class from its signature band; a debris cluster marked as a planet adds a warning on the chart.

label: Present finished chart to bridge
human_steps: Walk the finished chart on the slate up to the bridge and find the watch officer
Stand where the officer can see the screen and lay the slate face up beside it
Walk through the chart's main bodies with a pointer, naming each one as you go
Answer the officer's questions on uncertain bodies and point to the sweep time
Note the officer's decision on the slate and any action asked
Save the presentation record with the time and the officer's name
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is presenting a chart clearly and answering questions without overclaiming certainty; failure is confident talk about uncertain bodies that leads the bridge to a wrong decision.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the chart to the bridge and points at each body in turn, with the officer's questions requiring a sweep time; claiming an unknown as certain triggers a rebuke.
fit_note: A form fill; the real presentation is a spoken walk-through of the chart with questions to answer.

label: Plot the shortest safe course to the drop point
human_steps: Read the drop point coordinates from the cargo manifest
Load the hazard map and the master chart side by side on the console
Draw candidate lines from the ship to the drop point, avoiding marked hazards
Check each line's clearance against the safety margin at its closest point
Pick the shortest line that keeps every margin above the limit
Save the course with its clearance numbers and submit it for navigation
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is weighing a short course against its clearance margin; failure is a shortest line that clips a hazard by a few units.
ideal_interaction: The player draws course lines on the chart and checks clearance at each closest point; a line inside the margin turns red and cannot be saved.

label: Mark hazards along the route
human_steps: Pick up the hazard stylus and walk to the nav screen with the route on it
Look along the route line for each known hazard marked on the older chart
Tap each hazard, then choose its class from the hazard menu
Mark the closest approach distance beside each hazard in the notes
Check that the route line passes the marked hazards at a safe distance
Confirm the marks with the navigator and save the marked route
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is placing each hazard mark accurately on the route and calling its class correctly; failure is a hazard left off the route or the wrong class that changes the threat level.
ideal_interaction: The player taps each hazard along the route, picks its class from the menu, and checks the closest approach; a hazard left unmarked causes the route to flash a warning.

label: Plot fastest course to the stricken ship, ignoring comfort margins
human_steps: Read the stricken ship's last known position and its drift vector from the signal log
Load the master chart and the hazard map and set the comfort margins to zero
Draw the fastest line to the ship's position and check it against the hazards
Accept a line that passes inside the hazard margin, marking the risk in the notes
Save the course and the risk note together so navigation sees the trade-off
Submit the course to navigation with the time of the last position fix
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is choosing the fastest line while being honest about the hazard risk it accepts; failure is a course that clips a hazard with no risk note for the navigator.
ideal_interaction: The player draws the fastest line to the ship, watches the risk meter rise as it nears hazards, and must write a risk note before submitting; submitting without a note is refused.

label: Update the plot as the target drifts
human_steps: Walk to the nav station and read the target's latest position on the nav screen
Compare the new position with the plot's predicted position from the last update
Redraw the intercept line from the ship to the new position
Check the new line against hazards and the drift error bar
Confirm the new plot with the navigator by voice before the burn
Log the update time and the new drift value on the plot slate
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is re-plotting promptly as the target moves while checking each new line against hazards; failure is a stale intercept line that misses the target.
ideal_interaction: The player redraws the intercept as the target icon moves, watching the drift error bar; a stale line that misses the moving target loses the intercept.

label: Calibrate chart database against sensor test pattern
human_steps: Load the test pattern file from the calibration shelf and check its id
Open the chart database alongside the pattern and align the reference stars
Measure each test star's position against its known value using the ruler
Adjust the database offset until the test stars sit inside the tolerance band
Run the pattern check again and confirm all test stars pass
Save the calibration record with the offset values and the pass count
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is adjusting the offset to fit the test stars without overfitting to one star; failure is a database tuned to the pattern that drifts on real sensor data.
ideal_interaction: The player nudges the offset dial and watches the test stars settle inside the tolerance band; overfitting one star pulls the others out of band.

label: Report position-fix accuracy to bridge
human_steps: Pull the last position-fix error log from the lab terminal before walking up
Walk to the bridge and wait for the navigator to free up a moment
Read out the mean error, the worst error and the fix count from your slate
Point to the error plot on the nav screen to show where the worst fix sat
Answer the navigator's question about whether the error is inside the safe limit
Log the report with the time and the navigator's acknowledgement
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is reporting the error numbers clearly and saying plainly whether they are inside the limit; failure is an error figure that hides the worst fix.
ideal_interaction: The player reads the mean and worst error from the log, then points to the worst fix on the error plot; hiding the worst figure gets corrected by the navigator.

label: Walk crew deck patrol
human_steps: Draw the badge and zapper from the duty locker and clip them on
Walk the corridor slowly, looking at each door seal for a gap or a scorch mark
Check each crew door's status light and note any door held open
Look into each open alcove and cargo locker for anything out of place
Check the airlock locker's latch and count the spare suits
Log the patrol with the deck number, time and any door or locker note
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is spotting an out-of-place item or failing seal on a routine walk without becoming complacent; failure is a missed open door or an unlogged out-of-place item.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the corridor, checks each door light and seal in turn, and taps any open door or unlatched locker; a missed door leaves a breach on the board.

label: Check internal sensors and force fields
human_steps: Sit at the security console and wake the lifeform board
Scan the board's crew and visitor blips against the duty roster
Pull up each force-field emitter's status and note the readings
Test each emitter by pulsing it and watching the field strength climb
Flag any dead sensor on the board with its location
Log the test results and the dead sensor list for engineering
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is reading the board for a real anomaly among normal blips and checking the emitter output; failure is an unflagged dead sensor or a field left weak.
ideal_interaction: The player scans the lifeform board, pulses each emitter and watches its strength climb, flagging any dead sensor; a missed dead sensor leaves a gap in the board.
fit_note: A bench game; the real work is a console board scan and emitter pulse test.

label: Armory and charger check
human_steps: Open the armory door and count the zappers in the rack by their serial tags
Check each zapper's charge light and note any that is not full
Walk the charger racks and see each charger's status lamp is green
Check the lock log against the key on the wall board
Sign the armory sheet with the count and any faulty charger
Lock the armory and check the door latch twice
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is counting every zapper and checking each charge, catching a dead charger before it matters; failure is a zapper signed out uncharged or a faulty charger missed.
ideal_interaction: The player counts each zapper, checks its charge light and each charger lamp in turn, and signs the sheet; signing with a missing zapper or a dark lamp costs points.

label: Brig cell check
human_steps: Walk the brig corridor and look through each cell's viewing port
Check the cell occupant is breathing and awake before moving on
Test the cell's field by holding the field probe to the wall and listening for the hum
Check the meal tray through the hatch and note if it was taken
Note any cell where the field hum is weak or the occupant is unresponsive
Log the cell round with the cell numbers and any note for the medic
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is noticing an unresponsive occupant or a weak field before it becomes a breakout or a medical emergency; failure is a missed weak field or an occupant left unchecked.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the cells, checks each occupant through the viewing port, and presses the field probe to the wall to hear the hum; a dead hum or an unresponsive occupant triggers an alert.

label: Routine deck patrol
human_steps: Pick up the patrol slate and the badge from the duty locker
Walk the quarters corridor at a steady pace and look ahead for anything unusual
Check each door's seal light and any crew member standing in the corridor
Look into a few open alcoves at random and note anything out of place
Tick the slate at each deck junction to show the round is complete
Log the round with the time and whether it was quiet
what_makes_it_hard: The job is a quiet watch where the skill is staying alert over a long dull round; failure is drifting through the corridor and missing a door left open.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the corridor and checks each seal light, ticking the slate at each junction; a skipped junction leaves the round incomplete.

label: Check force-field board
human_steps: Sit at the brig console and open the force-field summary page
Read each emitter's power line and note its steady or flickering state
Check the field's edge coverage on the board for any hole
Compare the board to yesterday's reading on the slate
Mark any emitter whose reading has drifted down over the day
Log the board check with the time and the drifting emitter list
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is noticing a slow power drop across the board compared with the previous day; failure is a field that weakens slowly while each single reading looks fine.
ideal_interaction: The player reads each emitter's power line against yesterday's value and marks a drifting one; a hole in the edge coverage is flagged in red.
fit_note: Bench game; the real check is comparing the force-field board against yesterday's readings on the console.

label: Secure the lab and sensor spaces
human_steps: Walk to the lab door and check the door's seal light is on
Look along the lab benches and the sensor racks for loose samples or open cases
Close each sample case and check its latch with a firm press
Walk the sensor spaces and check each rack's status lamp is steady
Set the lab lock and test it by trying the handle from outside
Sign the lockup sheet with the time and the lock status
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is making sure every case is latched and every lamp steady before locking up; failure is a case left open or a lock that does not hold.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the bench and sensor racks, pressing each case latch and checking each rack lamp, then tests the lab lock from outside; an unlatched case leaves the lockup incomplete.

label: Escort away team to transporter and back
human_steps: Meet the away team at the corridor junction and count them off by name
Walk them down the corridor to the transporter room and keep them in front of you
Check each person's badge and comm unit at the pad before they step on
Stand at the pad edge and watch the transporter cycle until the team is safe
Count the team back on the pad when it returns and check each badge again
Log the escort with the team names and the return time
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is counting every person on and off the pad and noticing a missing badge in a hurry; failure is a team member left on the pad or an unknown person returned.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the team to the pad, checks each badge and comm unit, and counts them back; an extra or missing person on the count raises an alert.

label: Sweep returned specimens for hazards
human_steps: Pick up the handheld scanner and turn it on at the lab bench
Lift each returned specimen case and hold it at arm's length
Pass the scanner head slowly over each case and watch the hazard meter
Read the meter for radiation, spores or chemical readings and note the peak
Set any case with a red reading on the hazard shelf and tag it
Log each case's peak reading and the tag status in the security sheet
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is scanning every case slowly enough to catch a low-level hazard without skipping a case; failure is a fast sweep that misses a spore reading.
ideal_interaction: The player passes the scanner over each case slowly while the hazard meter climbs; a fast pass misses the peak and lets a hazardous case through.
fit_note: Sample collection activity for the botanist; the real work is a handheld hazard scan of returned cases.

label: Inspect and seal cargo bay
human_steps: Walk the cargo bay and look at each crate stack for damage or a broken strap
Check each crate's seal and tag against the manifest on the slate
Press the seal in place and wait for the green light on the seal unit
Walk to the bay door and check its hinge and latch by hand
Close the bay door and turn the wheel until the lock light goes steady
Log the bay as sealed with the time and the seal count
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is finding a broken seal or strap before sealing the bay; failure is a bay sealed with a crate open or a broken latch that opens under load.
ideal_interaction: The player checks each seal and strap, presses the seal unit until its light turns green, and turns the door wheel; a broken latch refuses the lock.

label: Guard shuttlebay unload
human_steps: Take up the guard post at the shuttlebay door and face the unload area
Check each crate coming off the shuttle against the manifest name and tag
Watch the loaders' hands and tools and note any crate moved outside the line
Check each crew badge as it passes the door and hold anyone unbadged
Call out each crate count to the loaders so the total stays in sync
Log the unload with the crate total and any badge hold
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is watching the unload while checking badges and counts together without losing either; failure is an unbadged person slipping through or a crate that leaves the line uncounted.
ideal_interaction: The player holds the guard post, checks each badge at the door and each crate against the manifest, calling the count; an unbadged person at the door is held and logged.

label: Count manifest against sealed lockers
human_steps: Pick up the manifest and walk the stores aisle to the first sealed locker
Read the locker's seal number and check it matches the manifest line
Open the locker and count each item against the item count on the manifest
Close the locker and press its seal until the light turns green
Mark the manifest line as counted and note any short or extra item
Move to the next locker and repeat until the aisle is complete
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is counting every item by hand without skipping one or resealing a locker with a short count; failure is a short item missed in the count and signed off.
ideal_interaction: The player counts each locker's items against the manifest in turn and presses the seal; resealing with a short count triggers a discrepancy warning.

label: Post guard at sickbay door and keep corridor clear
human_steps: Take up the guard post at the sickbay door and check the corridor both ways
Keep the corridor clear by asking any loiterer to move along by name
Check each person entering sickbay has a medical pass on their badge
Hold any stretcher team at the door until the medic calls them through
Watch the corridor for crowding and call for backup if the line grows
Log the post with the time and the count of people held at the door
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is holding the door for the right people while keeping the corridor moving; failure is a stretcher blocked too long or an unpassed visitor let in.
ideal_interaction: The player holds the door, checks each medical pass, and lets stretchers through only on the medic's call; an unpassed visitor let in raises an alert.

label: Escort stretcher teams from transporter
human_steps: Meet the stretcher team at the transporter pad and count the patients
Walk the team along the corridor with the stretchers kept level
Clear a path by moving bystanders aside with a calm call
Check each patient's wristband against the pad list before the team moves on
Stop at each corridor junction and wait for the team to clear it
Log the escort with the patient count and the delivery time to sickbay
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is keeping a stretcher level and quick while checking each patient's identity; failure is a stretcher dropped at a junction or a patient handed over without a matching wristband.
ideal_interaction: The player walks the team down the corridor, checks each wristband against the pad list, and waits at junctions; a wristband mismatch stops the team until resolved.

label: Enforce quarantine line if ordered
human_steps: Take up position at the quarantine line taped across the sickbay door
Read the quarantine order on the slate and confirm the line is the right one
Stop each person approaching the line and check their pass and purpose
Turn back anyone without a quarantine pass and note their name
Hold the line steady when crew press forward and call for backup
Log the line hold with the time, the names turned back and the order number
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is holding a firm line when people push and checking passes without bending the order; failure is a line crossed by an unpassed person or an order applied to the wrong door.
ideal_interaction: The player holds the quarantine line, checks each pass as people approach, and turns back anyone without one; letting an unpassed person across breaks the quarantine.

label: Test force fields and internal sensors
human_steps: Sit at the brig console and open the field test rig
Bring up each force-field emitter one at a time and read its test strength
Run the internal sensor sweep across the brig and corridor and check each reading
Compare each emitter's test reading against its spec plate
Mark any emitter that falls outside spec or any sensor that stays silent
Save the test result with the emitter list and the sensor count
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is running each test to spec and telling a weak emitter from a silent sensor; failure is a weak field passed as good or a silent sensor left unflagged.
ideal_interaction: The player brings up each emitter on the test rig, reads its strength against the spec plate, and marks any out-of-spec emitter; passing a weak one lowers the test score.

label: Run a security alert drill
human_steps: Take the drill card from the armory wall and read the scenario and timing
Walk to the PA panel and set the alert tone for the drill
Press the drill button and start the timer on your slate
Watch the crew response on the corridor screens and note who reaches the muster point
Call the drill stand-down on the PA and read the response time from the slate
Log the drill with the response time and any crew missing from the muster
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is timing the alert and reading the crew response accurately without warning people in advance; failure is a drill that leaks its timing or a missing crew member unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: The player presses the alert on the PA, starts the response timer, and checks the muster list as crew arrive; a missing name when the timer ends is logged as a failure.

label: Verify armory chargers hold full charge
human_steps: Pick up the charge meter and walk to the charger rack
Pull one zapper from its charger and clip the meter's probe to its contacts
Read the charge level on the meter and compare it to the full mark
Put the zapper back on its charger and check the lamp goes to charging
Repeat for each charger, marking any that do not reach full in the test time
Log the charger results and send any faulty charger to engineering
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is reading a real charge level off the contacts and not trusting the lamp alone; failure is a charger whose lamp shows green while the zapper sits at half charge.
ideal_interaction: The player clips the charge meter to each zapper's contacts and reads the level against the full mark; a green lamp with a low meter reading flags the charger as faulty.

label: Check long-range sensor calibration
human_steps: Walk from the lab door to the long-range console and sit, waking the calibration monitor.
Open the overnight drift printout and read the three gain-drift columns line by line, noting which channel has walked out.
Pull the reference star's catalogued spectrum onto the second screen and overlay it on the live return.
Turn the gain trim knob in small detents while watching the offset line creep toward the zero marker.
Stop once drift sits inside the tolerance band on the bezel; a reversed offset past zero means you overshot.
Write the before and after values and your initials into the calibration log, then sign it.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging when the overlay is close enough without chasing noise; failure is quietly trimming drift to hide a real fault.
ideal_interaction: Hold the gain knob while a reference spectrum overlays the live trace; turn in fine detents until the offset line crosses zero, and sign only if it stays there for a few seconds.
fit_note: generic tuning; the real job compares a drift printout against a reference star before adjusting.

label: Review sensor anomaly queue
human_steps: Sit at the anomaly terminal and open the queue, reading the count and the oldest entry first.
Read each entry's confidence score and which sensor array raised it.
Sort the list by confidence, starting with the lowest, and open its raw trace.
Check whether the spike also appears on the forward and aft arrays at the same bearing.
Rerun the scan from the console with a narrower bandwidth and watch whether the spike survives.
Close entries that vanish on rerun with a written reason; escalate the ones that repeat to the bridge.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a real anomaly from an instrument artifact; failure is closing a real contact as noise or escalating noise and causing needless alarm.
ideal_interaction: Drag each anomaly card into a confidence bin, then narrow the bandwidth slider on its raw trace and keep the spike only if it reappears at the same bearing on both arrays.
fit_note: the queue sorts entries but never involves rerunning a scan or comparing arrays against each other.

label: Walk sciences stations
human_steps: Pick up the station clipboard at the lab door and walk to the first bench terminal.
Stand at the bench and ask the nearest tech for a verbal status on their current run.
Open each shelf bin and count the reagent vials against the stock sheet, noting any short or expired labels.
Walk through to the arboretum doorway and look at the tray tags for the day's planting schedule.
Write each request on the clipboard as a line with the station's name beside it.
Return to the lab door and hand the clipboard to the duty tech, initialled and dated.
what_makes_it_hard: Noticing a small stock shortfall or a mislabelled vial among many correct ones; failure is walking past a short bin that stops someone's next assay.
ideal_interaction: Carry the clipboard along a fixed route, stopping at each station to press its status button, then tap each shelf bin to count vials against the sheet and flag any that read short.

label: Verify hydroponics health with botanist
human_steps: Walk into the arboretum with the botanist and stop at the nutrient meter on the first tray.
Dip the handheld probe into the reservoir and read the pH and dissolved nutrient figures aloud.
Walk along the tray and lift leaves to inspect undersides for spotting, curling or grey fuzz.
Confirm the canopy oxygen sensor reads within its band at the tray's far end.
Ask the botanist whether any plant needs a second look, and note which tray and which leaf.
Record the tray numbers and readings on the arboretum sheet and sign the hydro line.
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting early blight on the underside of a leaf before it spreads; failure is calling a tray healthy when the fungus has already started.
ideal_interaction: Walk the tray row dipping the probe in each reservoir, then rotate each leaf with a tap to reveal its underside and press the blight mark only where a spot is actually visible.

label: Routine passive sweep and log
human_steps: Sit at the console and set the array to passive mode, leaving gain at its last trimmed value.
Watch the drift indicator scroll slowly across the top of the display without touching the controls.
Each time the trace crosses a marked line, press the log key and note the timestamp.
Keep an eye on the watch timer and log a status entry at each interval it chimes.
If drift creeps past the line, lift the gain cover and make one small correction, then log that too.
Send the log to the XO at the end of the watch and sign off the console.
what_makes_it_hard: Staying attentive through a long, quiet watch and catching a slow drift that never jumps; failure is letting drift grow unlogged until the scans are useless.
ideal_interaction: Keep a slow trace scrolling and press the log key each time it crosses a marker, resisting the urge to touch gain unless the drift line is breached.
fit_note: tune rewards adjusting; the real task is passive watching and logging with restraint.

label: Sensor officer reviews cartography updates
human_steps: Open the chart update feed at the lab console and read the list of revised star positions.
Pull up the current chart beside the update on the second screen.
For each updated star, compare its new coordinates with its charted point and note the offset.
Check the offset against the error ring printed for that star's survey class.
Approve the update where the offset sits inside the ring, and flag where it falls outside.
Save the approved edits to the master chart and close the feed.
what_makes_it_hard: Judging whether a moved star is a real correction or a mis-keyed coordinate; failure is approving a typo that sends the helm to a phantom star.
ideal_interaction: Lay the old and new charts side by side and drag each updated star marker onto its charted point, approving only those that land inside their error ring.
fit_note: a trend line shows change over time; the real job is comparing point positions against an error tolerance.

label: Brief sensor, carto and botany on survey targets
human_steps: Stand at the lab console and open the survey target list on the wall display.
Call the sensor officer, the cartographer and the botanist on the comm and confirm each one is listening.
Read each target's bearing, range and priority aloud into the open channel.
Mark which department covers which sector on the coverage grid, dragging the tag onto each sector.
Ask each head to repeat their sector back, and correct any sector that two of them have claimed.
Save the coverage grid and send it to the bridge as the briefing record.
what_makes_it_hard: Getting three busy heads to agree on coverage without gaps or overlaps; failure is a sector nobody scans or two teams wasting time on the same target.
ideal_interaction: Tap each department's channel to read out a target, then drag its coverage tag onto a grid sector, and fix any sector left empty or claimed twice before sending.
fit_note: classify sorts items into bins; a briefing is spoken coordination and allocating coverage.

label: Run primary deep scan of target
human_steps: Sit at the deep scan console and read the bridge's target bearing and range from the order card.
Enter the scan range, band and integration time on the parameter pad, copying them from the card.
Turn the bearing wheel by hand so the crosshair settles on the target, watching the lock light.
Press start and watch the integration counter climb while the signal-to-noise meter rises.
Hold until the meter clears its threshold line; ending early leaves a noisy result.
Write the scan ID, time and final SNR into the log and save the scan.
what_makes_it_hard: Waiting out a full integration instead of cutting it short when the target is dim; failure is saving a scan too noisy to use and losing the mission data.
ideal_interaction: Turn the bearing wheel until the crosshair locks onto the target, then press and hold the scan key while the SNR meter climbs, releasing only once it crosses the threshold line.
fit_note: the job is aiming the array and holding a timed integration, not sorting results.

label: Cross-check results with cartography
human_steps: Pull the finished deep scan output onto the lab console from the saved log.
Request the cartographer's chart of the same sector on the second screen.
Place each detected object's coordinates over its charted point and read the offset.
Confirm the spectral class from the scan matches the chart's listed class for that point.
Flag any object outside its tolerance ring or with a class mismatch, and note its scan line.
Mark the sector verified only once every flagged object has been resolved or explained.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a true mismatch from a small measurement offset; failure is passing unverified findings to the bridge as settled fact.
ideal_interaction: Drag each scan detection onto its chart point and confirm it against the tolerance ring; objects that fall outside the ring light red and must be resolved before the sector can be marked verified.

label: Deliver survey summary
human_steps: Walk from the lab to the readyroom and sit at the desk terminal with the scan log in hand.
Open the summary form and enter each target's name and its final scan ID.
Copy each finding's figures from the log one field at a time, reading each digit back before moving on.
Set the confidence level for every finding, with a note on any finding still unverified.
List the open questions the summary leaves unanswered at the bottom of the form.
Submit the summary to the XO and wait for the receipt to appear on the desk.
what_makes_it_hard: Copying exact figures and marking honest confidence without overselling a shaky result; failure is a transposed digit or a claim stated as certain when it is not.
ideal_interaction: Fill the summary form field by field, copying each figure from the scan log where a mistyped digit flashes red, and set a confidence dial per finding before submitting.

label: Scan cargo for contamination or unknown materials
human_steps: Walk to the cargo bay locker and pull on gloves and a sealed sample bag.
Open the manifest card for the crate you are about to inspect and read its declared contents.
Run the handheld reader along each crate seam and corner, stopping where the meter ticks.
Wipe a swab across the flagged seam, seal it in the bag and slot it into the reader.
Compare the spectral peak to the manifest's declared material and tag the crate as clear or suspect.
Return the swab to the locker and log the crate ID on the cargo sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Running the reader slowly enough to catch a faint leak at a seam; failure is loading a hazardous crate unchecked because the sweep was rushed.
ideal_interaction: Sweep the handheld reader along a crate seam at a steady pace; slow down over ticking spots and press the swab key to bag a sample before comparing the peak to the manifest.

label: Assess route for sensor hazards
human_steps: Open the planned course on the lab console and read the waypoints from the navigation request.
Pull the dust and radiation density map and lay it over the route.
Drag a hazard marker onto each dense band that crosses the path, noting its strength.
Measure the detour around each marked band against the original route's length.
Send the hazard list and detour options to navigation with each marker's coordinates.
Log the assessment time and confirm navigation has acknowledged it.
what_makes_it_hard: Deciding which faint bands are real hazards worth a detour; failure is navigation flying through a dense field that the sensors had already seen.
ideal_interaction: Drag waypoints along a course through a hazard field, and where a density band crosses the line, drop a hazard marker; the route is only sent once every band on the path is marked.

label: Analyse samples for the medical team
human_steps: Take the sealed sample vials from the cold rack and read each label against the medical request.
Load a vial into the spectrometer tray and close the lid until it clicks.
Start the run and watch the trace draw peaks across the wavelength axis.
Match each peak to the reference library, noting any peak with no match.
Write the matched compounds and the unmatched peaks on the results sheet.
Send the results to the chief medical officer with the vial IDs listed.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a real unmatched peak from a contamination peak; failure is a missed compound that leaves the doctors treating the wrong illness.
ideal_interaction: After the run, drag each peak on the trace onto the reference library line it matches, and mark any peak left unmatched as a finding for the medical team.
fit_note: classify sorts items; the real job is a timed instrument run followed by matching peaks.

label: Scan the relief destination for pathogens and radiation
human_steps: Open the relief destination's grid on the console and select the biological and radiation bands.
Sweep the scanner cone across the first sector in a slow, overlapping arc.
Watch the sector's band indicator and note any reading that crosses its threshold.
Move to the next sector only after the current one has been covered end to end.
Mark each hot sector red and each clear sector green on the grid.
Send the marked grid to the bridge with the safe corridor highlighted.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping the sweep overlapping so no sector is skipped; failure is a gap in coverage that lets the away team walk into a contaminated corridor.
ideal_interaction: Drag the scan cone across the grid in overlapping strokes, and only a fully swept sector turns green; a sector that flashes its threshold colour must be marked before the next one can be started.
fit_note: the job is a systematic sector-by-sector sweep, which classify does not capture.

label: Supply botanical medicinal stock if required
human_steps: Walk into the arboretum and find the requisition sheet pinned at the medicinal bed.
Kneel at the bed and match each plant's tag and leaf shape against the requisition list.
Use the snips to cut each requested stem at the marked node, leaving the leaf pair intact.
Place each cut stem in the cold bag and keep the bag's lid closed.
Count the stems against the requisition and note any plant that was short or unmarked.
Log the count and the bed number on the stock sheet and send it to the CMO.
what_makes_it_hard: Cutting at the right node so the plant keeps growing and the medicine keeps its potency; failure is cutting too high and killing the plant or taking the wrong species.
ideal_interaction: Hold the snips over a stem and tap the node marker to make the cut; cutting above or below the node or taking an unlisted plant costs stock and is flagged in the bag.

label: Full sensor array diagnostic
human_steps: Sit at the console and run the array's self-test, watching the channel list fill with results.
Read each channel's error code and note which channels show amber or red lamps.
Walk to the sensor rack at the back of the lab and find the module for the first faulty channel.
Pull the module out of its rack slot and seat it again, feeling it click into the backplane.
Rerun the self-test and confirm the channel now reads green.
Save the diagnostic log with the fault codes, the actions taken and the final status.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a loose module from a dead one before pulling the whole rack; failure is swapping good parts or missing a fault that surfaces mid-test.
ideal_interaction: Press each channel's test button on the readout board, read its error lamp, and for a faulty channel pull and reseat its module in the rack until the self-test lamp turns green.
fit_note: tuning adjusts a live signal; a diagnostic is a self-test, error-code reading and physical module reseating.

label: Verify lab and hydroponics systems
human_steps: Start at the lab's air scrubber panel and read its flow gauge against the marked band.
Walk to the coolant manifold and check its pressure needle sits in the green zone.
Move into the arboretum and read the grow-light output meter over the first tray.
Feel the hydro pump housing for abnormal vibration and listen for a grinding note.
Note every gauge reading and any value outside its band on the shakedown sheet.
Sign the sheet at the arboretum door and hand it to the XO.
what_makes_it_hard: Noticing a gauge needle that sits just inside the band but drifts across a shift; failure is signing off a system that is quietly failing.
ideal_interaction: Walk gauge to gauge tapping each one, and where a needle sits at the band edge, hold the tap to watch its drift before you accept the reading.
fit_note: a walk-and-tick checklist does not make the player watch for slow gauge drift or feel pump vibration.

label: Report shakedown findings
human_steps: Sit at the readyroom desk and open the shakedown findings form.
Copy each fault from the diagnostic log, one line per fault, with its channel and error code.
Select a severity for each fault, from cosmetic to mission-blocking.
Estimate the repair time for each fault from the parts list and the crew's current load.
Attach the diagnostic log ID and sign the form.
Submit the form to the XO and confirm that the defects list is now on the command queue.
what_makes_it_hard: Rating severity honestly rather than calling everything minor to finish the shift; failure is a mission-blocking defect marked cosmetic and left unfixed.
ideal_interaction: Enter each fault as a line, then slide its severity marker along a scale and type a repair time that the parts list constrains; submitting is blocked while any fault has no severity.

label: Run queued samples
human_steps: Walk to the workbench and take the next sample from the queue tray, reading its barcode.
Label the sample tube with the queue number and your initials, then label the rack slot to match.
Load the tube into the spectrometer tray and close the lid until the latch engages.
Start the run and watch the spectrum trace build on the screen.
Read the peak heights against the expected range printed on the queue card.
Record the result in the log, and if any peak is abnormal, flag it for a re-run.
what_makes_it_hard: Labelling twice and matching the tube to the queue card with no mix-ups; failure is a swapped sample that sends the wrong result up the chain.
ideal_interaction: Scan each tube's barcode, slot it into the spectrometer tray, and once the trace is drawn, compare each peak to its band on the queue card before saving.

label: Calibrate instruments
human_steps: Sit at the calibration console and load the reference standard from the cold shelf.
Insert the standard into the instrument port and start the reference run.
Watch the readout against the certificate values printed on the standard's card.
If the reading drifts, turn the adjustment screw in small steps and rerun until it matches.
Note the before and after readings and the standard's batch number in the calibration log.
Return the standard to the cold shelf and sign the bench sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Turning the adjustment screw only as far as the standard demands; failure is over-tuning the instrument so every later sample reads subtly wrong.
ideal_interaction: Insert the reference standard, then turn the adjustment screw in small clicks while the readout moves toward the card's certified value, locking the screw once the reading holds steady.

label: Swab and contamination log
human_steps: Pull on gloves and take the swab kit from the bench drawer.
Wipe the bench surface and the fridge door handle in a set pattern, one swab per zone.
Seal each swab in its labelled tube and place the tubes in the incubator rack.
Walk the tubes to the culture bench and check each plate for colour change or fuzzy growth.
Enter each zone's result in the contamination log as clear or growth.
If any plate shows growth, seal the bench and call the bridge.
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting faint growth on a plate that looks almost clean; failure is copying yesterday's log and letting real growth go unnoticed.
ideal_interaction: Wipe each bench zone with a swab, drop each tube into its incubator slot, then open each plate and tap any colony spot you actually see before writing the log.
fit_note: sample handling is close, but the swab-and-plate reading of faint growth is not what the game asks.

label: Routine sample queue and calibration
human_steps: Stand at the workbench and count the tubes still waiting in the queue tray.
Pick the next tube, label it, and load it into the bench instrument.
Run the sample and read the peak heights against the card's band.
While the instrument idles, glance at its drift indicator and note any creep in the log.
Walk the queue back to the tech's list and update the count.
Pass the bench to the next watch with the queue count and drift note written on the sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping up with a long queue while noticing slow instrument drift; failure is a growing backlog and drift that goes unseen until the results are wrong.
ideal_interaction: Feed tubes through the bench instrument one at a time, and between runs keep an eye on the drift marker, pressing the note key when it creeps past its mark.
fit_note: the job mixes queue counting with watching drift between runs, not just sample handling.

label: Restock reagents
human_steps: Walk to the stores locker and read the reagent shelf labels against the stock sheet.
Pull each low bottle and read its fill line against the level mark.
Pick the matching reagent from the resupply crate, checking the batch date on each bottle.
Carry the new bottles to the bench and place each one on the right shelf with the label facing out.
Tick each reagent on the restock sheet and write the new batch number beside it.
Send the restock request for any reagent that is still below the fill line.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading fill lines and batch dates accurately under time pressure; failure is running out of buffer mid-assay or loading an expired reagent.
ideal_interaction: Lift each low bottle to check its fill line against the mark, swap in a fresh one from the crate with a matching batch date, and set it on the right shelf.

label: Analyse sensor-collected samples
human_steps: Take the sealed sample container from the sensor team's drop slot and check its seal.
Open the container and load a measured aliquot into the analysis cell.
Start the assay and watch the response curve climb and settle.
Compare the curve's shape against the expected profile card for this sample type.
Write the measured values, the curve's shape and any anomaly into the results sheet.
Send the completed results to the chief sciences officer with the container ID.
what_makes_it_hard: Recognising a curve that looks right but has a subtle shoulder that marks contamination; failure is reporting a clean result that the sensor team's survey relies on.
ideal_interaction: Pipette an aliquot into the analysis cell, start the assay, and compare the rising curve to the profile card by dragging it over the trace; flag any shoulder you can see.
fit_note: classify sorts samples into bins; the job is running an assay and reading a curve shape.

label: Prepare and tag survey specimens
human_steps: Take the specimen list from the bridge order and find each specimen in the cold box.
Lift each specimen into a sealed tray, keeping it at the stated temperature.
Write the specimen ID on a tag and tie it to the container's handle, double-checking the number.
Place each container in the correct bay, noting the bay number on the list.
Seal the cold box and log the time, so the degradation clock starts from a known point.
Mark each entry on the list as tagged and send the list to the chief.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping each tag matched to the right specimen when several look alike; failure is a swapped tag that breaks the survey's chain of custody.
ideal_interaction: Pick each specimen from the cold box, write its ID on a tag, and tie it to the matching container's handle; a tag that does not match the list refuses to attach.

label: Send summary to bridge
human_steps: Sit at the lab console and open the summary form for the bridge.
Enter the specimen counts and the headline results from the results sheet.
Read each finding aloud as you type it, to catch a wrong figure by ear.
Attach the results sheet and mark any finding still awaiting confirmation.
Preview the message to see it fit the bridge's required layout.
Send it on the bridge channel and wait for the acknowledgement.
what_makes_it_hard: Summarising the findings honestly in few words without dropping a qualifier; failure is a missing caveat that makes a tentative result look certain.
ideal_interaction: Type each headline result into the summary form, and attach a caveat tag to any finding not yet confirmed before the send button unlocks.
fit_note: the send form is a text entry; the job is condensing verified results and calling out caveats.

label: Test incoming cargo for contaminants
human_steps: Walk to the cargo locker and take the sample kit and gloves.
Open the crate's seal and lift the first item from the crate, keeping it upright.
Swab the item's outer surface in a single stroke and seal the swab in a bag.
Slot the bag into the field reader and wait for the reading to settle.
If the reading is clear, tag the item and set it aside; if not, bag the whole item and seal the crate.
Log the crate ID, item count and result in the cargo log before moving to the next crate.
what_makes_it_hard: Staying methodical through a long manifest and not skipping a shielded item; failure is a contaminated item entering the ship untested.
ideal_interaction: Lift each crate item and draw a swab across its outer surface, slot it into the field reader and wait for the needle to settle before tagging it clear or sealing it.

label: Log inspection results
human_steps: Sit at the lab console and open the cargo inspection log.
Enter each crate ID and the item count from the cargo sheet.
Enter each item's reading and its clear or suspect tag from the field reader's printout.
Check that every crate ID on the sheet has a matching entry in the log.
Mark each crate's release status and note any sealed items.
Submit the log to the cargo chief and confirm the release queue has updated.
what_makes_it_hard: Matching every crate ID and reading to its printout without a single missed line; failure is a crate released or held on the wrong result.
ideal_interaction: Drag each crate's printout line onto its log entry; an unmatched crate blocks submission until its reading and status are assigned.
fit_note: a form entry is text-only; the job is reconciling each printout line against the sheet.

label: Run patient blood and tissue panels
human_steps: Take the patient's blood and tissue vials from the medical cold box, checking the patient ID on each.
Load the blood vials into the centrifuge and close the lid, setting the spin for the panel.
While it spins, walk to the workbench and label the tissue slides in the patient's sequence.
Pipette each sample onto its panel plate and seal the plate.
Run the panel on the bench reader and watch each well colour develop.
Record each marker's level in the patient chart and flag any result outside its range.
what_makes_it_hard: Keeping patient IDs straight across many vials and getting the pipette volume exact; failure is a wrong patient's result or a mis-pipetted well that skews the diagnosis.
ideal_interaction: Pipette a precise volume into each panel well, holding the pipette steady until the well is filled to its line, then run the reader and tap any well whose colour falls outside the panel range.
fit_note: the job is hands-on sample prep and pipetting, not classifying items.

label: Culture and pathogen ID
human_steps: Take the inoculated culture plates from the incubator and read the growth on each.
Pick a single colony with a sterile loop and streak it onto a fresh plate.
Place the plate under the microscope and adjust the focus until the cell shape is sharp.
Compare the cell shape and staining to the pathogen reference card.
Record the best-match organism and its confidence in the pathogen log.
Send the identification to the CMO and mark the culture as complete.
what_makes_it_hard: Choosing a clean single colony and reading the cell shape accurately; failure is picking a mixed colony and misidentifying the pathogen, so the outbreak is missed.
ideal_interaction: Pick a colony with the loop and streak it onto a fresh plate, then focus the microscope until the cell outline sharpens and match its shape to the reference card before logging the ID.
fit_note: identifying a pathogen means streaking, focusing a microscope and reading cell shape; classify only sorts.

label: Deliver results to sickbay
human_steps: Walk from the lab to sickbay with the results folder held flat.
Find the biobed for the patient and check the patient ID on the bed card.
Hand the results to the attending doctor and say the key finding aloud.
Point to the specific marker or organism on the printout that needs attention.
Wait for the doctor to confirm they have read it and ask any questions.
Log the handover time and the doctor's name on the lab's transfer sheet.
what_makes_it_hard: Making sure the right result reaches the right patient and is read before the doctor moves on; failure is results sitting in a tray while treatment is delayed.
ideal_interaction: Carry the results folder to the biobed, match the patient ID on its card, and hand the folder across; the handover only logs once the doctor taps to acknowledge the key finding.
fit_note: the real work is a physical in-person delivery and verbal handover, not filling a form.

label: Test lab instruments under load
human_steps: Sit at the lab console and start the load test, which runs all instruments at high throughput.
Watch each instrument's status lamp and throughput counter climb.
Read the temperature and pressure gauges on the instrument stack for any upward creep.
Note the first instrument that drops out or shows an error.
Stop the test, shut the failing instrument down and pull its maintenance log.
Record each instrument's result, the time it failed, and the load it was under.
what_makes_it_hard: Catching a fault in an instrument that is still running but overheating; failure is an instrument that dies mid-maneuver with a sample still in it.
ideal_interaction: Start the load test, then keep the throughput dials at the top of their range while watching each instrument's temperature gauge, pulling the load off the first instrument whose needle enters red.
fit_note: a bench test is a static run; the real job is watching heat and error under a rising load.

label: Secure samples for hard maneuvers
human_steps: Walk to the workbench and read the list of samples that need securing.
Place each sample tube into a padded holder and snap the holder's lid shut.
Lock each holder into its slot in the transit rack, feeling for a firm click.
Test each holder by giving the rack a gentle shake to check nothing moves.
Tighten any holder that rattles until the rack sits still.
Sign the transit list and note the rack's slot numbers.
what_makes_it_hard: Getting every holder fully latched so none rattles in a hard turn; failure is a loose holder that spills or smashes a sample when the ship manoeuvres.
ideal_interaction: Place each tube into a padded holder, lock it into its rack slot until it clicks, then shake the rack and tighten any holder that rattles.

label: Long-range sweep and contact log
human_steps: Sit at the science console and bring up the long-range sweep display.
Start the sweep and watch the returns paint across the bearing ring.
Filter out the background noise band by band until the true returns stand clear.
Tag each contact with its bearing, range and estimated size, and note any that are new since the last sweep.
Log each contact in the contact list and confirm the count matches the display.
Send the sweep summary to the bridge, stating whether any contact is new.
what_makes_it_hard: Separating faint real contacts from background noise without filtering them out; failure is a real contact lost to an over-eager filter or a ghost logged as a ship.
ideal_interaction: Sweep the bearing ring and tap each bright return to tag it, then pull the noise filter slider until the background dims and only real contacts stay lit.
fit_note: tuning adjusts a signal; the job is sweeping, filtering noise and tagging contacts into a list.

label: Lateral array alignment
human_steps: Sit at the console and pull the lateral array's drift data for the last shift.
Read the bearing error for each of the array's elements against the reference grid.
Nudge the alignment control for the worst element in small steps.
Aim the array at the reference star and check the return brightness and position.
Repeat the nudge and test until the element sits in tolerance.
Sign the alignment log with the final error figures.
what_makes_it_hard: Making small corrections without overshooting and without ignoring a slow drift; failure is an array that is aligned on a single test but drifts off within the watch.
ideal_interaction: Hold the alignment control and nudge it while the reference star's return must sit centred in its crosshair; release once the bearing error falls inside the tolerance band.

label: Lifeform scanner spot check
human_steps: Sit at the lifeform scanner and pull up the ship's current crew roster.
Run a lifesign sweep of the decks, watching the count climb deck by deck.
Compare each deck's count against the roster's expected headcount for that deck.
Flag any deck where the count is short, over or reading blank.
Walk the flagged deck's count again to confirm the mismatch before reporting it.
Log the mismatch with the deck and count, and tell the bridge if the discrepancy stands.
what_makes_it_hard: Telling a real missing crew member from a scanner glitch; failure is ignoring a real gap or calling the bridge over a glitch that a second sweep would clear.
ideal_interaction: Sweep the deck tiles in turn, and compare each deck's live count to its roster number; a mismatch stays flagged until a second sweep of that deck either confirms or clears it.
fit_note: the job is counting lifesigns against a roster and rechecking mismatches, not classifying.

label: Review lab tech work
human_steps: Walk to the lab workbench and read the sample queue sheet pinned beside it.
Check each tech's finished sample tubes for correct labels and seals.
Look at the log entries for the day's runs and confirm each one has a result and an initial.
Assign the next queued sample to whichever tech is free, writing their name on the queue.
Sign off each finished run on the sheet, with your initials and the time.
Hand any run that looks wrong back to its tech with a note on what to recheck.
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting a mislabelled tube or a missing result without re-running everything yourself; failure is signing off a bad run that then misleads the bridge.
ideal_interaction: Walk the bench tapping each finished tube's label and seal, then sign off each run only if its log line has a result and an initial; a bad run is handed back with a note.

label: Routine sweep and drift check
human_steps: Sit at the console and set the array to routine sweep mode.
Watch the sweep draw its ring and note any return that is faint or new.
Check the array's drift indicator and log its reading at each interval.
If a faint return persists across two passes, mark it for a second look.
If drift creeps toward its limit, adjust the gain one step and log the change.
Pass the sweep log to the next watch with the drift figure written on it.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding attention through quiet sweeps while spotting a faint return that appears only once; failure is missing a contact that builds slowly until it is close.
ideal_interaction: Keep the sweep ring turning and tap any faint return to mark it, then press the drift check key at each interval and nudge gain only when the drift line is crossed.
fit_note: tune rewards adjusting; the real job is watching a quiet sweep for faint returns and logging drift.

label: Report all-clear to bridge
human_steps: Walk from the lab to the bridge and step up to the sensor console.
Read the latest sweep log and confirm the time of the last clear sweep.
Give the bridge the all-clear with the sweep time and the drift figure.
Say the range of the sweep so the bridge knows how far the all-clear reaches.
Wait for the bridge's acknowledgement before stepping away.
Note the report time and the officer who acknowledged it in the log.
what_makes_it_hard: Saying all-clear only when the sweep truly covers the stated range; failure is an all-clear that the bridge trusts while a corner of space is unscanned.
ideal_interaction: Walk to the bridge console and read the sweep log's range and time aloud, then press the all-clear key only once the range you stated matches the sweep's coverage.
fit_note: the report is a physical walk-up and spoken all-clear, not a form.

label: Aim arrays at survey target
human_steps: Read the target's bearing and range from the bridge order card.
Turn the array's pointing wheel toward the bearing while watching the scale tick over.
Adjust the elevation dial to the target's declination and read the scale to confirm.
Watch the lock indicator and steady the wheel until the target's return centres on the crosshair.
Lock the array and log the bearing, elevation and lock time.
Report to the bridge that the arrays are aimed and locked on the target.
what_makes_it_hard: Steadying the wheel so the lock holds without drifting off the target; failure is survey data that is thin or smeared because the array slipped.
ideal_interaction: Turn the pointing wheel and elevation dial until the return sits on the crosshair, then hold the wheel steady until the lock light holds green for a full count.
fit_note: tune adjusts a signal's parameters; the job is physically aiming arrays with dials and holding lock on a moving target.

label: Run full-spectrum scan and bracket
human_steps: Set the scan to the full band and start the sweep at the lower end of the spectrum.
Watch the spectral trace fill and note where the target's peaks appear.
Bracket each peak by setting a lower and upper frequency cursor either side.
Narrow each bracket until the peak's shape stops changing with each pass.
Save each bracketed peak to the scan record with its range and strength.
Report to the cso that the full-spectrum bracket is complete.
what_makes_it_hard: Setting each bracket tight enough to capture the peak without clipping its shoulders; failure is a clipped peak that gives the cso a wrong composition.
ideal_interaction: Drag a pair of frequency cursors either side of each spectral peak, narrowing them until the peak's shoulders sit just inside; clipping a shoulder turns the bracket red.
fit_note: the job is bracketing and narrowing spectral peaks, which classify does not capture.

label: Package survey data for the bridge
human_steps: Walk to the bridge console and pull the survey scan records from the science station.
Sort the contacts by bearing and merge duplicates from the two sweeps.
Strip the raw noise frames from the package, keeping only the bracketed findings.
Write a one-line description beside each finding in plain language.
Check each finding's confidence tag and attach the caveat where the data is weak.
Send the package to the bridge's tactical screen and confirm it has loaded.
what_makes_it_hard: Removing the noise without throwing out a faint but real contact; failure is a package that buries the bridge in raw frames or drops a faint contact.
ideal_interaction: Drag each raw frame into the noise bin, and merge duplicate contacts onto one entry; a contact with a weak confidence tag must carry its caveat before the package can be sent.
fit_note: packaging merges and filters raw records into findings; verify compares a value against a reference.

label: Sweep approach lanes for debris
human_steps: Sit at the console and read the approach lanes from the bridge's route order.
Set the debris sweep to the lane's width and bearing.
Run the sweep along the lane, watching for small returns that move against the background.
Mark each debris return with its size and speed, and note the lane's clear distance.
Send the debris list to navigation with the closest return's range and bearing.
Log the sweep as complete for the lane and move to the next.
what_makes_it_hard: Spotting a small slow-moving debris return against a busy background; failure is unseen debris on the lane that hits the hull at speed.
ideal_interaction: Run the debris sweep along the lane and tap any small return that moves against the background to tag it; the lane only clears once the closest tagged return is sent to navigation.
fit_note: the job is sweeping a lane and tracking moving returns, not classifying a finished scan.

label: Scan cargo for hazardous signatures
human_steps: Walk to the cargo door and take the handheld hazard scanner from its holster.
Hold the scanner at arm's length and step along the crate line at a steady pace.
Sweep the scanner's head slowly across each crate's door seam, watching for the signature light.
When the light shows amber, stop and bring the scanner in close to the seam to confirm.
Mark the crate's ID and the signature type on the cargo ticket.
Report any hazardous crate to the ops officer and hold it in the door before it loads.
what_makes_it_hard: Holding a steady sweep rate while catching a faint leak at a crate seam; failure is a leaking container that loads and spreads its signature into the ship.
ideal_interaction: Sweep the handheld scanner slowly along each crate seam; where the signature light ticks amber, bring the head in close and hold it until the light settles before marking the crate.
fit_note: the job is a live hand-held sweep for leaks at seams, not taking and running a sample.

label: Locate the target vessel and lifesign count
human_steps: Sit at the console and open the target vessel's last known position from the bridge order.
Aim the lifesign array at the vessel and wait for the return to appear.
Filter the return to remove the vessel's hull noise and isolate the lifesigns.
Count the lifesign points, moving the count cursor across each cluster.
Estimate the vessel's deck layout from the cluster positions.
Send the lifesign count and vessel position to the bridge with a confidence figure.
what_makes_it_hard: Separating a dense lifesign cluster into individual people without double counting; failure is a wrong count that leaves the relief team unprepared.
ideal_interaction: Aim the lifesign array at the vessel, then drag the count cursor across each cluster, tapping each point once and marking any point that sits inside a cluster already counted.
fit_note: counting clustered lifesigns and avoiding double counts is a tracked count, not a class assignment.

label: Relay lifesign data to sickbay
human_steps: Pull the vessel's lifesign count and cluster map from the science console.
Open the relay channel to sickbay and wait for the medical desk to answer.
Read each cluster's count and location aloud, one at a time, so the doctors can write it down.
Ask the medical desk to read back the total and each cluster figure.
Correct any figure the medical desk reads back wrongly, and repeat that cluster.
Log the relay time and the sickbay officer's name when they confirm.
what_makes_it_hard: Reading figures aloud clearly and catching a misheard number on the read-back; failure is sickbay preparing the wrong number of beds.
ideal_interaction: Pick each cluster on the map and send it down the relay channel, then wait for the read-back and tap any figure that does not match your count before the relay closes.
fit_note: the job is a spoken relay with a read-back check, not decoding a signal.

label: Watch for hazards around the vessel
human_steps: Sit at the console and set the proximity alarm to a radius around the target vessel.
Watch the proximity display for any new object entering the radius.
Estimate each new object's speed and bearing from its track on the display.
Flag any object closing faster than the threshold, and say so on the bridge comm.
Keep the radius clear and tell the bridge the moment a hazard enters it.
Log each hazard with its time of entry and its closest approach.
what_makes_it_hard: Catching an object that enters the radius quietly and closes fast; failure is a surprise hazard at close range while the relief team is aboard.
ideal_interaction: Watch the proximity display and, when a new object enters the radius, drag its track line to estimate its speed; flag any object whose line crosses the threshold before it reaches the vessel.
fit_note: the job is continuous proximity watching and tracking closing speed, not classifying objects.

label: Full array calibration against reference
human_steps: Sit at the console and load the reference target's specification from the calibration file.
Point the full array at the reference target and wait for the return to lock.
Read each element's return against the reference figures, one element at a time.
Adjust each element that falls outside its band, using the alignment control and rechecking after each change.
Confirm every element sits inside tolerance on a final pass.
Sign the calibration record and note the time and the reference used.
what_makes_it_hard: Working through every element with patience and not stopping at the first passing one; failure is a single bad element that quietly ruins the whole array's results.
ideal_interaction: Point the array at the reference target, then go element by element, nudging each alignment control until its return bar sits inside the tolerance band before moving to the next.

label: Report range and resolution figures
human_steps: Walk to the bridge console and bring up the calibration record from the science station.
Read the array's maximum detection range and its resolution figure from the record.
Check each figure against the range the bridge needs for the mission.
Give the bridge the range and resolution figures out loud, stating which elements were tested.
Note any element that could not be tested and why.
Log the report time and the bridge officer who received it.
what_makes_it_hard: Quoting range and resolution honestly, including the figure for an element that failed; failure is the bridge trusting an optimistic range and misjudging readiness.
ideal_interaction: Walk to the bridge console and read the range and resolution figures from the calibration record, then press to send only once every untested element has been listed with its reason.
fit_note: the report is a spoken, in-person handover of figures, not a form entry.

label: Ward rounds
human_steps: Walk the biobed row from the bay doors, reading each patient's wristband and bed slate before touching anyone.
Lay a hand on each forehead and two fingers on the carotid, counting pulse against a sweep second hand for fifteen seconds.
Read the tricorder vitals and compare them with the chart; a respiration rate creeping from 14 to 22 is the thing to catch.
Speak to each patient directly, asking where the pain sits and whether they slept, and note the answer on the slate.
Amend orders on the slate, marking any changed dosage in red so the night nurse cannot miss it.
Brief the duty nurse at the station, pointing at the bed by number, before moving on.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is spotting the patient whose numbers look fine but whose manner has changed; failure is a missed deterioration that surfaces hours later.
ideal_interaction: Player walks the biobed row holding the tricorder, sweeping each patient for vitals, then picks the one whose trend has drifted; a wrong pick lowers the readiness score.

label: Medical stores and drug audit
human_steps: Unlock the controlled-drug locker with a thumb plate and log the time in the access ledger.
Lift each hypo cassette and read the batch code and expiry date engraved on its base.
Count the sealed vials by tapping them out onto the tray in rows of ten, not by eye.
Compare each count to the ledger; a single vial short means opening the cabinet below to look for a fallen one.
Break the seal on one sterile pack and check the indicator strip turned colour, rejecting any that did not.
Enter requisition quantities on the stores terminal, then sign the ledger page with the stylus.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is a count that reconciles exactly against the ledger; failure is a silent discrepancy that leaves a controlled drug unaccounted for.
ideal_interaction: Player tallies vials out of the locker onto the tray in tens, one tap per vial, and the ledger total must match; a wrong total or an expired batch left on the shelf fails the audit.

label: Check the medical hologram
human_steps: Walk to the EMH emitter alcove and open its maintenance hatch with the flat driver.
Hold the diagnostic probe to the emitter lens and watch the calibration grid for offset rings.
Run the emitter diagnostic on the console and read the drift figure in millimetres for each axis.
Step in front of the projector and ask three protocol questions, listening for a delayed or misquoted answer.
Correct the drift with the fine adjustment wheel until the grid rings close concentrically.
Log the final drift and protocol result; a drift above two millimetres gets a flagged note and a re-run.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is hearing the small lag in a spoken answer and reading slight drift; failure is a hologram that answers wrongly in an emergency.
ideal_interaction: Player aims the diagnostic probe at the emitter lens and turns the fine-adjust wheel to close the calibration rings, then answers the protocol quiz at the console; a ring left open or a missed answer leaves the drift flagged.

label: Crew health screening
human_steps: Collect sealed sample vials from the sickbay tray and carry them to the lab bench.
Label each vial with the crewman's ID and draw time, reading the label back against the chart.
Load the vials into the centrifuge rack, balancing opposite positions by weight.
Read the haematocrit and white-count bars on the analyser, noting fatigue markers against last month.
Plot each crewman's trend line and look for a steady slide across three screenings rather than one bad number.
Flag at-risk names on the screening sheet and send the list to the XO with a one-line reason for each.
what_makes_it_hard: The judgement is reading a slow trend across many people; failure is flagging one noisy result or missing a creeping decline.
ideal_interaction: Player loads sample vials into the centrifuge with balanced weights, then draws each crewman's counts onto a trend graph and drags a flag onto anyone sliding over three screenings.
fit_note: Vitals is a single-patient reading; the job is comparing trends across a crew from lab samples.

label: Routine physicals for one department
human_steps: Pick up the department roster and walk to the biobed with the first named crewman.
Ask them to sit on the bed edge and tilt their head so you can look inside the ear with the otoscope.
Press the stethoscope to the chest in four places, counting breaths for thirty seconds at each.
Check the reflex by tapping the knee with the reflex hammer and watching the foot.
Ask about sleep, diet and any pain, and write the answers in the physical form in the crewman's own words.
Sign the clearance line only if all four checks are normal; flag any elevated reading instead.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is running four routine checks cleanly while noticing the odd sign; failure is a rushed check that clears someone with a murmur.
ideal_interaction: Player moves the stethoscope to four chest positions in turn, holding each for a breath count, and taps the reflex hammer at the knee; a skipped spot or a clearance signed over a flagged reading fails the physical.

label: Drug audit and requisition
human_steps: Open the drug cabinet and pull the controlled-substances register from its clip.
Count each shelf of hypos and ampoules, reading the expiry dates against the register.
Pull out any vial past its date and bag it in red hazard tape for disposal.
Work out the reorder for each low line: par level minus count, rounded up to a full box.
Enter the requisition on the stores terminal and confirm the order number printed on the slip.
Initial the register and file the slip in the clear sleeve; the audit is incomplete until both are done.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is reconciling counts against par and dates without rounding errors; failure is ordering the wrong quantity or leaving expired stock on the shelf.
ideal_interaction: Player works the shelves, pulling expired vials into a disposal bag by reading each date, then types the reorder quantity as par minus count; a wrong figure or an expired vial left shelved costs the requisition.

label: Health summary to captain
human_steps: Walk to the bridge console and wait for the captain's acknowledgement tone before speaking.
Pull up the readiness summary and read each crewman's status from the sickbay board.
Select the three items that would change the captain's decision: unfit numbers, any outbreak, bed count.
Type the summary in plain language, giving every figure a unit and a time stamp.
Read the summary aloud to the captain, watching for a nod or a question before you finish.
Submit the form with the sickbay log attached; a summary missing a time stamp is returned for correction.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is choosing the few facts that change a decision and stating them plainly; failure is burying the captain in figures or leaving out a bad trend.
ideal_interaction: Player picks three facts from the readiness board for the summary form's priority slots and reads them to the captain; leaving out the outbreak line or sending a bare number fails the brief.
fit_note: A form fills fields, but the real work is choosing what matters and saying it aloud to the captain.

label: Prepare away-team medical kits
human_steps: Take the kit list from the wall and walk to the sealed kit cabinet.
Pull one trauma kit at a time and tip it onto the bed, checking each item against the list.
Check each sterile pack's seal and indicator strip; rejected packs go into the sealed bin.
Pack the kit in tiered order, bandages and tourniquets on top and drugs in the lidded case below.
Snap the case shut, check the locking tab, then tape the colour code to the lid.
Load the kit onto the transporter trolley and sign the release slip for the away team.
what_makes_it_hard: The judgement is spotting an incomplete or compromised kit before it leaves; failure is a team that goes out missing a tourniquet or carrying a broken seal.
ideal_interaction: Player moves each item from the tray into the kit case in tiered order and rejects a torn seal before closing the lid; a missing item or a closed kit with a bad seal fails the pack.

label: Screen away team for fitness
human_steps: Call each away-team member to the biobed in the order on the manifest.
Read their baseline from the wristband and the last physical before any test begins.
Have them walk the length of the bay and back, watching for a limp or an uneven gait.
Clip the oximeter to a fingertip and note the blood oxygen figure once it settles.
Ask about any illness, medication or sleep deficit in the last thirty-six hours.
Stamp the clearance card fit, conditionally fit or unfit, and tell the team leader the reason.
what_makes_it_hard: The skill is judging readiness from a short walk and a quiet answer; failure is clearing someone sick enough to go down on the surface.
ideal_interaction: Player walks each team member across the bay while watching their gait, then clips the oximeter to the fingertip and stamps the clearance card; a fit stamp over a low oxygen reading fails the screen.

label: Analyse exotic samples for contamination hazard
human_steps: Take the sealed sample canister from the transfer port and read the containment tag.
Open the containment cabinet and place the sample in the sealed bench well through the gloves.
