Wipe the sensor glass with a dry cloth and reseat the sample tray.
Note a pass or a drift for each unit on the round sheet.
Report any drifting unit to the quartermaster before moving on.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is spotting a slow drift in a readout that still says pass; failure is a food unit sliding out of spec and sending wrong meals to the galley.
ideal_interaction: Sensor sweep: the player moves a sensor wand across each food unit's glass in round order, comparing the colour readout to the golden card and marking any unit whose colour drifts.
fit_note: bench is a workbench-style test; routine checks are a walked round of units.

label: Stores count and refill
human_steps: Walk to the stores locker and pick up the tally card.
Open each hopper bin and count the canisters inside.
Pull canisters from the locker shelf and drop each one into its hopper slot.
Circle any hopper that is still under the fill line after the drop.
Write the totals on the tally card.
Hand the card to the quartermaster at the stores door.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is counting quickly and noticing a hopper still below the line; failure is a hopper running dry during a later surge.
ideal_interaction: Canister drop: the player takes canisters from the locker shelf and drops each one into the matching hopper slot, and a hopper still under the fill line after the drop is flagged.
fit_note: a tally fits the count, but refilling hoppers by drop is the real job and is missing.

label: Prepare sample containers and lab consumables on industrial replicator
human_steps: Walk to the workshop workbench and load the sample container pattern.
Set the batch count from the science request sheet.
Start the print and wait for the first container to exit the slot.
Take each container off the tray and check it is free of stray filament.
Snap a lid onto each container and press it down until it clicks.
Stack the sealed containers into the lab crate and label the crate.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is seeing a stray filament or a lid that did not seat; failure is a container that leaks sample on the lab bench.
ideal_interaction: Lid snap: the player takes each printed container, checks for stray filament, and presses the lid down until it clicks, with a loose lid counted as a failed container.

label: Extra rations for long lab shifts
human_steps: Walk to the mess replicator and read the shift roster on the wall panel.
Count one ration pattern per tech and enter the total on the touch screen.
Check each ration's nutrition tag on the output tray.
Bag the rations by shift and seal each bag.
Write the shift number and tech name on each bag label.
Stack the bags by shift at the lab door.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is entering the right count per tech and noticing a nutrition tag that does not match; failure is a lab tech getting too few rations on a long shift.
ideal_interaction: Roster count: the player sets the printed quantity per tech from the roster list before pressing print, and a count that does not match the roster is rejected.
fit_note: fresh does not involve roster counts or matching the nutrition tags.

label: Pattern buffer check after sensor power draw
human_steps: Walk to the mess replicator after the sensor power spike and read the power meter.
Open the service hatch with the panel key.
Attach the probe to the buffer and run the check.
Compare the buffer's trace to the baseline card taped inside the hatch.
Flush the buffer only if the trace drifts outside the baseline band.
Log the check and the power reading in the unit book.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is telling a harmless post-spike wobble from a corrupted pattern; failure is missing a corrupt pattern that surfaces as a meal with the wrong taste.
ideal_interaction: Spike then baseline: the player waits out a power spike on the meter, then compares the buffer waveform to the baseline overlay and flushes only the traces that fall outside the band.

label: Print pallet straps and crate seals
human_steps: Walk to the workshop workbench and read the manifest for the strap lengths.
Load the strap pattern into the industrial replicator.
Set the length to the manifest figure and start the print.
Lift the printed strap and check its width against the gauge.
Cut the strap to length with the shears at the marked line.
Stack the straps and seals on the cargo cart and count them against the manifest.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is sizing a strap to the pallet and noticing a width that is too thin to hold; failure is a strap that snaps under load.
ideal_interaction: Length cut: the player sets the strap length from the manifest, prints it, then cuts the printed strap at the mark with the shears, and a cut off the line is rejected.

label: Reconcile matter stores against manifest
human_steps: Walk to the matter locker and pull the manifest sheet from the clip.
Read the first manifest line and find the matching canister on the shelf.
Scan the canister's label and tick the manifest line.
Move each scanned canister to the done shelf so it is not counted twice.
Compare the total count to the manifest total at the end of the sheet.
Report any shortage to the quartermaster with the line number.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is tracking which canister has already been counted; failure is a double count that hides a shortage until a later crisis.
ideal_interaction: Scan and move: the player scans each canister label against the manifest line and moves it to the done shelf, and a canister scanned twice counts as a shortage.

label: Print medical consumables and sterile packs
human_steps: Walk to the workshop workbench and load the sterile pack pattern.
Check the sterilisation indicator strip on the replicator output tray.
Start the print and take each pack from the output tray as it finishes.
Place each pack in a sterile tray and lay a seal strip across the flap.
Press the packed tray into the seal press and hold until the indicator strip turns green.
Label the tray with the print time and send it to sickbay.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is catching a pack whose indicator never turned green; failure is an unsterile pack reaching a wound.
ideal_interaction: Seal hold: the player lays each packed tray in the seal press and holds the press down until the indicator strip turns green, and a release before the green counts as an unsterile pack.
fit_note: sequence covers printing but not the sterility indicator check and the seal press.

label: Bland meal batch for relief patients
human_steps: Walk to the mess replicator and read the sickbay bland diet order.
Select the bland meal pattern and set the batch count to the patient total.
Check each patient's allergen tag on the order and confirm the pattern has none of those ingredients.
Start the batch and take a portion for the temperature check.
Portion the meal into the patient trays and cover each tray.
Stack the trays on the cart by patient bed number.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is catching an allergen the pattern hides; failure is giving a patient a meal that makes them ill.
ideal_interaction: Allergen gate: the player scans each patient's allergen tag and must reject any pattern containing a flagged ingredient before the print button unlocks for that batch.

label: Keep pharmacy replicator feedstock clean
human_steps: Walk to the sickbay pharmacy and put on gloves.
Open the replicator hatch and check the feed nozzle for residue.
Take a swab and wet it with solvent from the bottle.
Wipe along the feed nozzle in one stroke, then check the swab for colour.
Repeat the wipe until the swab comes away clean.
Close the hatch, record the cleaning time, and sign the log.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is knowing when the nozzle is clean, which the swab shows; failure is residue left in the feed, contaminating the next dose.
ideal_interaction: Nozzle swab: the player holds a solvent swab against the feed nozzle and wipes in one stroke, and the swab's residue indicator must read clean before the hatch can close.

label: Run full diagnostics on every replicator unit
human_steps: Walk the mess replicator line in order, from the unit by the door.
Open each unit's service panel with the panel key.
Attach the test rig to the unit's diagnostic port.
Hold the test button until the sub-test LEDs go steady.
Read the fault code card for any LED that stays red and note it.
Close the panel and move on to the next unit.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is holding the test long enough for a slow fault to show; failure is skipping a unit so a fault surfaces under load later.
ideal_interaction: Stepped test line: the player moves the test rig from unit to unit and holds each unit's test button until its LEDs go steady, and a unit released early leaves its fault hidden.

label: Spare parts printed for engineering
human_steps: Walk to the workshop workbench and read the engineering order.
Load the spare part pattern into the industrial replicator.
Start the print and wait for the part to finish.
Lift the part and file the burrs off its edges with the file.
Drop the part into the fit gauge and check it seats without play.
Box and label the part for engineering.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is telling a part that seats from one that rattles; failure is a spare that fails to fit when engineering needs it under repair.
ideal_interaction: File and gauge: after the print finishes, the player files the burrs off the edges and drops the part into the fit gauge, where any play in the slot marks the part as failed.
fit_note: sequence is a generic print-then-wait; spare parts need a fit check against the engineer's gauge.

label: Report power draw anomalies from the units
human_steps: Walk to the stores console and pull up the power trend graph for each unit.
Scan each trace for spikes above the baseline band.
Mark the time of each spike that is not explained by startup.
Cross-check the marked times against the unit's job log.
Write the anomaly report with unit number, time and peak.
Send the report to the bridge from the console.
what_makes_it_hard: Judgement is telling a startup spike from a real overload; failure is a real overload going unreported until a unit burns out.
ideal_interaction: Trend scrub: the player drags a timeline across each power trace and taps the spikes above the baseline band, leaving startup spikes unflagged.
